title.zh: 卷五十六 吳書十一 朱治朱然呂範朱桓傳
title.en: Volume 56: Book of Wu 11 - Biographies of Zhu Zhi, Zhu Ran, Lü Fan, and Zhu Huan
title.raw: 卷五十六 吳書十一 朱治朱然呂範朱桓傳 Volume 56: Book of Wu 11 - Biographies of Zhu Zhi, Zhu Ran, Lü Fan, and Zhu Huan

sentences.zh: 朱治字君理，丹楊故鄣人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Zhi, courtesy name Junli, was a native of Gucheng in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhi, styled Junli, came from Gucheng in Danyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 初為縣吏，後察孝廉，州辟從事，隨孫堅征伐。

translations.literal: At first he served as a county clerk; later he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, the province summoned him as an Attendant Clerk, and he followed Sun Jian on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a county clerk, then earned recommendation as Filial and Incorrupt, was recruited by the province as an Attendant Clerk, and marched with Sun Jian on his expeditions.

sentences.zh: 中平五年，拜司馬。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of the Zhongping era, he was appointed major (sim).
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongping 5 (188 CE) he received appointment as major.

sentences.zh: 從討長沙、零、桂等三郡賊周朝、蘇馬等。

translations.literal: He followed (Sun Jian) in attacking the bandits Zhou Chao, Su Ma, and others in the three commanderies of Changsha, Lingling, and Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the campaign against the bandit leaders Zhou Chao and Su Ma across Changsha, Lingling, and Guilin.

sentences.zh: 有功，堅表治行都尉。

translations.literal: For his merit, Jian memorialized the throne that Zhi should act as commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When he distinguished himself, Sun Jian submitted a memorial recommending Zhu Zhi for acting commandant.

sentences.zh: 從破董卓於陽人，入洛陽。

translations.literal: He followed (Sun Jian) in defeating Dong Zhuo at Yangren and entered Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Sun Jian to the victory over Dong Zhuo at Yangren and then entered Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 表治行督軍校尉，特將步騎，東助徐州牧陶謙討黃巾。

translations.literal: (Sun Jian) memorialized that Zhi should act as colonel who directs the army; he was specially given command of infantry and cavalry and went east to assist the provincial governor of Xu Province, Tao Qian, in attacking the Yellow Turbans.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian had him named acting colonel who directs the army, gave him independent command of foot and horse, and sent him east to help Tao Qian, governor of Xu Province, crush the Yellow Turbans.

sentences.zh: 會堅薨，治扶冀策，依就袁術。

translations.literal: When Jian died, Zhi supported Sun Ce and attached himself to Yuan Shu.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Jian died, Zhu Zhi steadied the young Sun Ce and threw in his lot with Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 後知術政德不立，乃勸策還平江東。

translations.literal: Later, realizing that Shu's governance and virtue would not stand, he urged Ce to return and pacify the lands east of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Yuan Shu could never establish legitimate rule, he persuaded Sun Ce to turn back and conquer the territory east of the river.

sentences.zh: 時太傅馬日碑在壽春，辟治為掾，遷吳郡都尉。

translations.literal: At that time the grand tutor Ma Midi was at Shouchun; he summoned Zhi as a staff member and promoted him to commandant of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: While the grand tutor Ma Midi was at Shouchun, he recruited Zhu Zhi onto his staff and then advanced him to commandant of Wu.

sentences.zh: 是時吳景已在丹楊，而策為術攻廬江。

translations.literal: At this time Wu Jing was already in Danyang, while Ce was attacking Lujiang on behalf of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jing already held Danyang for their side, even as Sun Ce was besieging Lujiang on Yuan Shu's orders.

sentences.zh: 於是劉繇恐為袁、孫所並，遂構嫌隙。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liu Yao, fearing that he would be swallowed up by Yuan and Sun, sowed suspicion and estrangement.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao, afraid the Yuan–Sun alliance would absorb him next, began picking quarrels and driving wedges between the allies.

sentences.zh: 而策家門盡在州下，治乃使人於曲阿迎太妃及權兄弟。

translations.literal: Ce's entire household was still downriver in the provincial capital, so Zhi sent men to Qu'e to escort the grand consort and Quan and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: With Sun Ce's family still trapped below the capital at the provincial seat, Zhu Zhi dispatched men to Qu'e to bring the Lady Dowager and the young Sun brothers to safety.

sentences.zh: 所以供奉輔護，甚有恩紀。

translations.literal: Thus the support, supply, and protection he afforded them were deeply felt and meticulously kept.
translations.idiomatic: He fed them, guarded them, and kept good order around them; the kindness was remembered in every detail.

sentences.zh: 治從錢唐欲進到吳，吳郡太守許貢拒之於由拳，治與戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Zhi set out from Qiantang intending to press on into Wu; the grand administrator of Wu, Xu Gong, barred his path at Youquan, but Zhi fought him and routed him badly.
translations.idiomatic: Marching from Qiantang toward Wu, he was blocked at Youquan by Xu Gong, the grand administrator of Wu; Zhu Zhi attacked and shattered Xu Gong's force.

sentences.zh: 貢南就山賊嚴自虎，治遂入郡，領太守事。

translations.literal: Gong fled south to join the mountain bandit Yan Zihu, whereupon Zhi entered the commandery and took charge of the grand administrator's duties.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gong fled south into the hills to the bandit chief Yan Zihu, and Zhu Zhi entered the commandery and assumed the governor's office.

sentences.zh: 策既走劉繇，東定會稽。

translations.literal: After Ce had driven off Liu Yao, he pacified Kuaiji to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sun Ce had expelled Liu Yao, he secured Kuaiji in the east.

sentences.zh: 權年十五，治舉為孝廉。

translations.literal: When Quan was fifteen, Zhi recommended him as Filial and Incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan turned fifteen, Zhu Zhi put him forward as Filial and Incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 後策薨，治與張昭等共尊奉權。

translations.literal: Later, when Ce died, Zhi joined Zhang Zhao and others in honoring and supporting Quan.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Ce's death, Zhu Zhi stood with Zhang Zhao and the rest to raise Sun Quan as their lord.

sentences.zh: 建安七年，權表治為

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jian'an, Quan memorialized the court that Zhi should be appointed as
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jian'an (202 CE), Sun Quan memorialized the throne to appoint Zhu Zhi as

sentences.zh: （九真）

translations.literal: (Jiu Zhen)
translations.idiomatic: (the commandery of Jiu Zhen—an alternate reading noted in brackets—)

sentences.zh: 太守，行扶義將軍，割婁、由拳、無錫。

translations.literal: grand administrator, acting general who upholds righteousness, excising Lou, Youquan, and Wuxi
translations.idiomatic: grand administrator with the acting title General Who Upholds Righteousness, carving out Lou, Youquan, and Wuxi

sentences.zh: 毗陵為奉邑，置長吏。

translations.literal: and Piling as his support fief, and installing chief officials.
translations.idiomatic: together with Piling as his fiscal domain, where he installed magistrates to administer the towns.

sentences.zh: 征討夷越，佐定東南，禽截黃巾余類陳敗、萬秉等。

translations.literal: He campaigned against the Yi and Yue peoples, helped stabilize the southeast, and captured or cut down the remnant Yellow Turban bands led by Chen Bai and Wan Bing.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against the southern tribes, helped secure the southeast, and mopped up Yellow Turban holdouts such as Chen Bai and Wan Bing.

sentences.zh: 黃武元年，封毗陵侯，領郡如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangwu, he was enfeoffed as marquis of Piling and continued to hold the commandery as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangwu 1 (222 CE) he received the marquisate of Piling while remaining governor of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 二年，拜安國將軍，金印紫綬，徙封故鄣。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed general who stabilizes the state, with a gold seal and purple ribbon, and his fief was moved to Gucheng.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was named general who stabilizes the state, given the gold seal and purple ribbon, and transferred his enfeoffment to Gucheng.

sentences.zh: 權歷位上將，及為吳王，治每進見，權常親迎。

translations.literal: As Quan ascended through the ranks of senior commander and then became king of Wu, whenever Zhi came for an audience Quan would invariably go out to greet him in person.
translations.idiomatic: As Sun Quan rose from field command to kingship of Wu, he would personally come out to welcome Zhu Zhi every time Zhu arrived for audience.

sentences.zh: 執版交拜，饗宴贈賜，恩敬特隆，至從行吏，皆得奉贄私覿，其見異如此。

translations.literal: He would take the tablet in both hands and bow in exchange, feasting him, granting gifts, and showing singular favor and respect, so that even the attendants who accompanied him on his rounds were allowed to present private gifts and pay their respects—such was the exceptional treatment.
translations.idiomatic: He clasped his tablet, bowed in return, lavished banquets and gifts on him, and singled him out for deference so marked that even Zhu Zhi's escort clerks might offer personal gifts and be received—an honor almost without parallel.

sentences.zh: 初，權弟翊，性峭急，喜怒快意，治數責數，諭以道義。

translations.literal: At first Sun Quan's younger brother Sun Yi had a harsh, impatient temper and indulged his moods of joy and anger; Zhi repeatedly reproved and admonished him, instructing him in the way of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan's younger brother Sun Yi had a sharp temper and often gave way to impulse; Zhu Zhi scolded him more than once and reasoned with him about what honor required.

sentences.zh: 權從兄豫章太守賁，女為曹公子婦，及曹公破荊州，威震南土，賁畏懼，欲遣子入質。

translations.literal: Quan's cousin Sun Ben, grand administrator of Yuzhang, had given his daughter in marriage to a son of Lord Cao; when Lord Cao overran Jing Province and his prestige shook the south, Ben grew afraid and wished to send a son as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ben, Sun Quan's cousin and governor of Yuzhang, had married his daughter to a son of Cao Cao; after Cao Cao crushed Jing Province and his name thundered across the south, Sun Ben panicked and wanted to send a son south as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 治聞之，求往見賁，為陳安危，

translations.literal: When Zhi heard of it, he asked leave to go see Ben and set forth for him the balance of safety and peril,
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Zhu Zhi begged permission to visit Sun Ben and lay out for him how much stood to be lost or gained,

sentences.zh: 〈江表传载治说贲曰：“破虏将军昔率义兵入讨董卓，声冠中夏，义士壮之。

translations.literal: The Jiang Biao Zhuan records Zhi's persuasion of Ben as follows: "The General Who Smashes Fugitives once led a righteous host west to punish Dong Zhuo, and his fame crowned the Central Plains—men of honor still thrill at the tale.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang Biao Zhuan preserves Zhu Zhi's words to Sun Ben: "Your father the General Who Smashes Fugitives once marched in the righteous host against Dong Zhuo, and his name topped the heartland; gallant men still speak of it with pride.

sentences.zh: 讨逆继世，廓定六郡，特以君侯骨肉至亲，器为时生，故表汉朝，剖符大郡，兼建将校，仍关综两府，荣冠宗室，为远近所瞻。

translations.literal: The General Who Pacifies Rebels succeeded him, widened his sway across six commanderies, and because you, my lord, are bone and flesh of the house and a vessel born for the age, he therefore memorialized the Han court, split the tall tally for a great commandery, and at the same time set up generals and colonels, linking both offices—glory that crowned the imperial clan and made you the cynosure of near and far.
translations.idiomatic: The General Who Pacifies Rebels carried on his work, brought six commanderies to heel, and, because you are the nearest of kin and a man the times require, had you written into the Han registers with a great commandery, joint command of two bureaus, and honors that outshone every other prince of the blood—you became the man everyone watched.

sentences.zh: 加讨虏聪明神武，继承洪业，揽结英雄，周济世务，军众日盛，事业日隆，虽昔萧王之在河北，无以加也，必克成王基，应运东南。

translations.literal: Add to that how the General Who Captures Fugitives is astute and godlike in war, has inherited the great enterprise, gathers heroes, and succors the age: his armies grow daily and his achievement mounts, so that even Prince Xiao of Han on the north bank of the Yellow River could not surpass him. He is sure to complete the royal foundation and answer the omens of the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan besides is brilliant and formidable in arms, has taken up the great legacy, rallies able men, and mends the world's troubles; his hosts swell by the day and his cause towers higher—even Liu Xiu in his Hebei days never outshone him. He will finish the work of kingship and fulfill Heaven's mandate in the southeast.

sentences.zh: 故刘玄德远布腹心，求见拯救，此天下所共知也。

translations.literal: That is why Liu Xuande has opened his heart from afar and begged rescue—this is known throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Liu Bei, from far away, has laid bare his inmost heart and pleaded for deliverance—the whole realm knows it.

sentences.zh: 前在东闻道路之言，云将军有异趣，良用怃然。

translations.literal: Earlier, when I was in the east, I heard talk on the road that you, General, were inclining another way, and I was deeply dismayed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while I was still in the east, travelers' gossip said you were leaning toward another master, and the news left me heartsick.

sentences.zh: 今曹公阻兵，倾覆汉室，幼帝流离，百姓元元未知所归。

translations.literal: Now Lord Cao blocks the armies, has overturned the house of Han, the young emperor wanders homeless, and the common people, countless as they are, have nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: Today Cao Cao holds the hosts at bay, has all but pulled down the Han, the boy emperor is driven from pillar to post, and the black-haired millions have no refuge.

sentences.zh: 而中国萧条，或百里无烟，城邑空虚，道殣相望，士叹於外，妇怨乎室，加之以师旅，因之以饥馑，以此料之，岂能越长江与我争利哉？

translations.literal: The heartland lies desolate—sometimes a hundred li without smoke; towns stand empty and the starving lie dead along the roads; gentlemen sigh in the fields and wives lament indoors; add armies on top of that and famine in their train, and by this reckoning how could they ever cross the Long River to vie with us for advantage?
translations.idiomatic: The central plain is a wasteland: for miles no cooking fires, cities hollow, corpses lining the ditches, scholars groaning in the wilds, women weeping indoors—and still more troops march and famine follows. Judge from that: could they really cross the Yangzi and wrest profit from us?

sentences.zh: 将军当斯时也，而欲背骨肉之亲，违万安之计，割同气之肤，啖虎狼之口，为一女子，改虑易图，失机毫釐，差以千里，岂不惜哉！”〉

translations.literal: At such a moment you, General, would turn your back on your own flesh and blood, abandon a plan that brings ten thousandfold safety, cut the skin shared by the same breath, and feed your flesh to tigers and wolves—for the sake of one woman you would change your mind and shift your design; miss the moment by a hair's breadth and you will be a thousand li astray—could that be anything but a waste?"
translations.idiomatic: And you, General, at such an hour would betray your kin, spurn the one course that keeps you safe, slice flesh from your own bone, and drop it into the maw of wolves—for one woman's sake you would swap your whole strategy; a hair's miss now becomes a thousand li of regret. Would that not be a bitter loss?"

sentences.zh: 賁由此遂止。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ben for this reason desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ben dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 權常歎治憂勤王事。

translations.literal: Quan often sighed that Zhi worried and toiled for the kingly enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan often remarked how Zhu Zhi wore himself out in the service of the state.

sentences.zh: 性儉約，雖在富貴，車服惟供事。

translations.literal: His nature was frugal; even amid wealth and honor his carriages and robes only sufficed for duty.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly: even at the height of rank his equipage and dress were only what the office required.

sentences.zh: 權優異之，自令督軍御史典屬城文書，治領四縣租稅而已。

translations.literal: Quan treated him with extraordinary favor, personally ordering the supervising army clerk and the clerk in charge of capital documents to handle routine paperwork while Zhi merely collected the land tax of four counties.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan singled him out for favor, had the supervising army clerk and the metropolitan registrar take over the paperwork, and left Zhu Zhi only the rent and tax of four counties to administer.

sentences.zh: 然公族子弟及吳四姓多出仕郡，郡吏常以千數，治率數年一遣詣王府。

translations.literal: Yet the sons of the ducal houses and the four great clans of Wu mostly took office in the commandery, so that clerks in the bureau often numbered in the thousands; Zhi would every few years dispatch a batch to the royal residence.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the great Wu lineages filled the commandery staff until the clerks ran into the thousands; Zhu Zhi still sent several hundred of them up to court every few years.

sentences.zh: 所遣數百人，每歲時貢獻御，權答報過厚。

translations.literal: The several hundred men he sent would each season present tribute for the imperial household, and Quan's return gifts were always lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Those hundreds brought seasonal tribute to the palace, and Sun Quan's gifts in reply were always munificent.

sentences.zh: 是時丹楊深地，頗有奸叛，亦以年向老，思戀土風，自表屯故鄣，鎮扶山越。

translations.literal: At that time the interior of Danyang was deep country with much treachery and rebellion; also because he was growing old and longed for the customs of his native soil, he memorialized on his own authority to garrison Gucheng and pacify the mountain Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Danyang's hinterland was rife with defection, and Zhu Zhi, feeling his years, yearned for home; he therefore asked to camp at Gucheng and keep the mountain Yue in check.

sentences.zh: 諸父老故人，莫不詣門，治皆引進，與共飲宴，鄉黨以為榮。

translations.literal: Not one of the village elders or old friends failed to call at his gate, and Zhi admitted them all, drinking and feasting with them, so that the township reckoned it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Every elder and old comrade came to his door, and he welcomed them all to drink and feast until the whole countryside glowed with pride.

sentences.zh: 在故鄣歲餘，還吳。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year at Gucheng, he returned to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He spent just over a year at Gucheng, then went back to the capital at Wu.

sentences.zh: 黃武三年卒，在郡三十一年，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangwu he died; he had been in the commandery thirty-one years and was sixty-nine sui.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Huangwu 3 (224 CE) after thirty-one years in the commandery, aged sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子才，素為校尉領兵，既嗣父爵，遷偏將軍。

translations.literal: His son Cai had long served as a colonel with troops; after inheriting his father's noble rank he was promoted to lieutenant general.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu Cai had already commanded troops as a colonel; when he inherited the title he advanced to lieutenant general.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：才字君业，为人精敏，善骑射，权爱异之，常侍从游戏。

translations.literal: The Book of Wu states: Cai, courtesy name Junye, was by nature keen and alert, skilled in horsemanship and archery, and Quan loved him for it and kept him constantly at his side for sport.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu shu adds: Zhu Cai, styled Junye, was quick-witted and a superb horseman and bowman; Sun Quan doted on him and kept him always at hand for the hunt.

sentences.zh: 少以父任为武卫校尉，领兵随从征伐，屡有功捷。

translations.literal: In youth, by his father's position, he became a colonel of the martial guard, led troops and followed the expeditions, and repeatedly won success.
translations.idiomatic: While still young he entered the martial guard colonelcy through his father's rank, led men on campaign, and won distinction again and again.

sentences.zh: 本郡议者以才少处荣贵，未留意於乡党，才乃叹曰：“我初为将，谓跨马蹈敌，当身履锋，足以扬名，不知乡党复追迹其举措乎！

translations.literal: Critics in his home commandery thought that at so young an age he occupied such glory and rank that he paid no heed to his township; Cai then sighed and said, "When I first became a commander I thought that straddling a horse and treading on the enemy, bearing the brunt myself, would be enough to make a name; I did not know that the township would still trace my every step!
translations.idiomatic: Men at home murmured that a boy so highly placed snubbed local opinion; Zhu Cai sighed, "When I first took command I believed that riding straight at the foe and catching every blade on my own shield would win me fame—I never guessed my neighbors would still judge every move I make!

sentences.zh: ”於是更折节为恭，留意於宾客，轻财尚义，施不望报，又学兵法，名声始闻於远近。

translations.literal: "Thereupon he changed his conduct to humility, attended carefully to guests, prized righteousness over wealth, gave without expecting return, and also studied the art of war, so that his reputation began to be heard far and near.
translations.idiomatic: "So he mended his manners, cultivated guests, spent freely for honor's sake without counting the cost, and took up military science until his name carried up and down the roads.

sentences.zh: 会疾卒。〉

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 才弟紀，權以策女妻之，亦以校尉領兵。

translations.literal: Cai's younger brother Ji; Quan gave him Sun Ce's daughter in marriage, and he too led troops as a colonel.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Zhu Ji married a daughter of Sun Ce on Sun Quan's arrangement and likewise commanded men as a colonel.

sentences.zh: 紀弟緯、萬歲，皆早夭。

translations.literal: Ji's younger brothers Wei and Wansui both died young.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ji's younger brothers Zhu Wei and Zhu Wansui both died young.

sentences.zh: 才子琬，襲爵為將，至鎮西將軍。

translations.literal: Cai's son Wan inherited the noble rank and became a general, rising to general who guards the west.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Cai's son Zhu Wan inherited the marquisate, served as a general, and rose to general who guards the west.

sentences.zh: 朱然字義封，治姊子也，本姓施氏。

translations.literal: Zhu Ran, courtesy name Yifeng, was his elder sister's son and had originally borne the surname Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ran, styled Yifeng, was Zhu Zhi's nephew by his elder sister and had been born into the Shi clan.

sentences.zh: 初治未有子，然年十三，乃啟策乞以為嗣。

translations.literal: At first Zhi had no son; when Ran was thirteen, he petitioned Ce to take him as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhu Zhi long had no heir, when the boy turned thirteen Zhu Zhi begged Sun Ce to let him adopt Zhu Ran as his successor.

sentences.zh: 策命丹楊郡以羊酒召然，然到吳，策優以禮賀。

translations.literal: Ce ordered the Danyang commandery to summon Ran with sheep and wine; when Ran arrived at Wu, Ce treated him with ceremony and congratulated him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce told the Danyang authorities to welcome Zhu Ran with the ritual sheep and wine; when the youth reached Wu, Sun Ce received him with full courtesy and congratulations.

sentences.zh: 然嘗與權同學書，結恩愛。

translations.literal: Ran once studied letters together with Quan and they formed a bond of affection.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ran had studied the classics side by side with Sun Quan, and the two grew close.

sentences.zh: 至權統事，以然為餘姚長，時年十九。

translations.literal: When Quan took charge of affairs, he appointed Ran magistrate of Yuyao; at the time he was nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan assumed leadership he named Zhu Ran magistrate of Yuyao; Zhu was nineteen.

sentences.zh: 後遷山陰令，加折沖校尉，督五縣。

translations.literal: Later he was moved to magistrate of Shanyin, with the added title colonel who breaks the charge, supervising five counties.
translations.idiomatic: He was later shifted to magistrate of Shanyin with the additional rank of colonel who breaks the charge, overseeing five counties.

sentences.zh: 權奇其能，分丹楊為臨川郡，然為太守，

translations.literal: Quan marveled at his ability, split off Danyang to form Linchuan commandery, and made Ran grand administrator,
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan, impressed by his talent, carved Linchuan commandery out of Danyang and made him its governor,

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：此郡寻罢，非今临川郡。〉

translations.literal: Pei Songzhi notes: That commandery was soon abolished; it is not the present Linchuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi remarks: that commandery was abolished shortly afterward and is not the Linchuan of later ages.

sentences.zh: 授兵二千人。

translations.literal: and assigned him two thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He was given two thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 會山賊盛起，然平討，旬月而定。

translations.literal: When mountain bandits suddenly rose in force, Ran pacified and attacked them, and within a month or so order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain bandits erupted; Zhu Ran struck them down and had the region quiet within a month.

sentences.zh: 曹公出濡須，然備大塢及三關屯，拜偏將軍。

translations.literal: When Lord Cao came out to Ruxu, Ran prepared a great dock and garrisons at the three passes, and was appointed lieutenant general.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao advanced on Ruxu, Zhu Ran built a great pier and fortified the three passes, and received appointment as lieutenant general.

sentences.zh: 建安二十四年，從討關羽，別與潘璋到臨沮禽羽，遷昭武將軍，封西安鄉侯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Jian'an he followed the campaign against Guan Yu; separately, together with Pan Zhang, he reached Linju and captured Yu, whereupon he was promoted general who displays martial prowess and enfeoffed as village marquis of Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 24 (219 CE) he joined the expedition against Guan Yu, then with Pan Zhang pushed separately to Linju, took Guan Yu alive, and was raised to general who displays martial prowess and enfeoffed as village marquis of Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 虎威將軍呂蒙病篤。

translations.literal: The fierce tiger general Lü Meng lay gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: The fierce tiger general Lü Meng was dying.

sentences.zh: 權問曰："卿如不起，誰可代者?"蒙對曰："朱然膽守有餘，愚以為可任。

translations.literal: Quan asked, "If you cannot rise again, whom can I appoint in your place?" Meng replied, "Zhu Ran's courage in defense is more than sufficient; in my humble opinion he can be entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan asked him, "If you do not recover, who could replace you?" Lü Meng answered, "Zhu Ran's nerve for holding a line is ample; I would deem him fit for the post.

sentences.zh: "蒙卒，權假然節，鎮江陵。

translations.literal: "When Meng died, Quan lent Ran the credentials of office and stationed him at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Meng died, Sun Quan gave Zhu Ran the imperial baton and left him to guard Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 黃武元年，劉備舉兵攻宜都。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangwu, Liu Bei raised troops and attacked Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangwu 1 (221 CE) Liu Bei marched against Yidu.

sentences.zh: 然督五千人與陸遜並力拒備。

translations.literal: Ran directed five thousand men and joined Lu Xun in resisting Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ran led five thousand men and stood with Lu Xun to block Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 然別攻破備前鋒，斷其後道，備遂破走。

translations.literal: Ran separately smashed Bei's vanguard and severed his rear route, so that Bei was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ran on a separate wing shattered Liu Bei's van and cut his line of retreat, and Liu Bei broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 拜征北將軍，封永安侯。

translations.literal: He was appointed general who campaigns north and enfeoffed as marquis of Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was named general who campaigns north and enfeoffed as marquis of Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 魏遣曹真、夏侯尚、張郃等攻江陵，魏文帝自住宛，為其勢援，連屯圍城。

translations.literal: Wei sent Cao Zhen, Xiahou Shang, Zhang He, and others to attack Jiangling; Emperor Wen of Wei himself stayed at Wan to back their momentum, linking camps in a ring around the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wei dispatched Cao Zhen, Xiahou Shang, Zhang He, and others against Jiangling; Cao Pi of Wei camped at Wan to stiffen their thrust, and their camps ringed the walls.

sentences.zh: 權遣將軍孫盛督萬人備州上，立圍塢，為然外救。

translations.literal: Quan sent the general Sun Sheng to lead ten thousand men to hold the islet in the river, erecting stockades and a dock to serve as outside relief for Ran.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sent General Sun Sheng with ten thousand men to hold the midriver islet, building palisades and a pier as an outer lifeline for Zhu Ran.

sentences.zh: 郃渡兵攻盛，盛不能拒，即時欲退，郃據州上圍守，然中外斷絕。

translations.literal: He ferried troops across to attack Sheng; Sheng could not withstand him and wished to withdraw at once, but He seized the stockade on the islet and held it, so that Ran was cut off inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He threw troops across to hit Sun Sheng, who could not hold and tried to fall back; Zhang He took the islet fort, and Zhu Ran was completely isolated.

sentences.zh: 權遣潘璋、楊粲等解而圍不解。

translations.literal: Quan sent Pan Zhang, Yang Can, and others to relieve the siege, yet the siege would not lift.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sent Pan Zhang, Yang Can, and others to break the ring, but the Wei lines held firm.

sentences.zh: 時然城中兵多腫病，堪戰者裁五千人。

translations.literal: At that time many soldiers in Ran's city were swollen with sickness; those fit to fight were barely five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the city disease had swollen the soldiers' limbs; scarcely five thousand could still bear arms.

sentences.zh: 真等起土山，鑿地道，立樓櫓臨城，弓矢雨注，將士皆失色，然晏如而無恐意，方厲吏士，伺間隙攻破兩屯。

translations.literal: Zhen and the others raised earthen hills, dug tunnels, set siege towers overlooking the walls, and poured down arrows like rain; the officers and men all lost color, yet Ran was calm as a banquet and showed no fear, and only then did he sternly rouse his clerks and soldiers, watch for a gap, and storm two camps.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei generals piled earthworks, drove tunnels, raised lofted towers above the walls, and shot until the arrows fell like rain; Zhu Ran's men went white with terror, yet he himself sat as calmly as at a feast, showed not a trace of panic, then roused officers and men, waited his opening, and stormed two enemy camps.

sentences.zh: 魏攻圍然凡六月日，未退。

translations.literal: The Wei assault ringed Ran for six full months and still did not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: For half a year the Wei army invested Zhu Ran without lifting the siege.

sentences.zh: 江陵令姚泰領兵備城北門，見外兵盛，城中人少，谷食慾盡。

translations.literal: The Jiangling magistrate Yao Tai led troops to guard the north gate; seeing how strong the enemy outside was and how few the men inside were, he thought the grain would soon be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangling magistrate Yao Tai held the north gate; seeing the enemy's numbers and the thinning garrison, he believed the grain would give out.

sentences.zh: 因與敵交通，謀為內應。

translations.literal: Therefore he communicated with the foe and plotted to act as an inside collaborator.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore opened secret talks with the enemy and plotted to betray the city from within.

sentences.zh: 垂發，事覺，然治戮泰。

translations.literal: When it was on the very point of breaking out, the affair was discovered, and Ran investigated and executed Tai.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was discovered on the eve of the blow; Zhu Ran tried Yao Tai and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 尚等不能克，乃徹攻退還。

translations.literal: Shang and the others could not overcome him, so they broke camp and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Shang and his colleagues could not force the city, so they struck their camps and retired.

sentences.zh: 由是然名震於敵國，改封當陽侯。

translations.literal: From this Ran's name shook the enemy states, and his fief was changed to marquis of Dangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ran's name thereafter struck terror in the rival courts, and his fief was moved to the marquisate of Dangyang.

sentences.zh: 六年，權自率眾攻石陽，及至旋師，潘璋斷後。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Sun Quan personally led the host to attack Shiyang; when the army turned back, Pan Zhang covered the retreat.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Huangwu Sun Quan himself led a great host against Shiyang; on the march home Pan Zhang commanded the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 夜出錯亂，敵追擊璋，璋不能禁。

translations.literal: They issued from the camp at night in disorder, the enemy pursued Zhang, and Zhang could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: The night march came out in confusion; the foe chased Pan Zhang, and he could not check them.

sentences.zh: 然即還住拒敵，使前船得引極遠，徐乃後發。

translations.literal: Ran at once turned back to hold off the enemy, letting the leading ships run out to the utmost distance before he himself weighed anchor last.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ran wheeled about to screen the retreat, letting the van ships pull far ahead before he cast off last of all.

sentences.zh: 黃龍元年，拜車騎將軍、右護軍、領兗州牧。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huanglong he was appointed chariot and horse general, right protector of the army, and concurrently shepherd of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Huanglong 1 (229 CE) he became chariot and horse general, right protector of the army, and nominal shepherd of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以兗州在蜀分，解牧職。

translations.literal: Before long, because Yan Province lay in Shu territory, the shepherd's office was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yan Province was reckoned to fall within Shu's partition of the realm, so the shepherd title was stripped.

sentences.zh: 嘉禾三年，權與蜀剋期大舉，權自向新城，然與全琮備受斧鉞，為左右督。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiahe, Quan and Shu set a joint date for a great offensive; Quan himself advanced on Xincheng, while Ran and Quan Zong received the battle-axes and acted as left and right directors.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiahe 3 (234 CE) Sun Quan and Shu agreed on a grand offensive: Sun Quan marched on Xincheng while Zhu Ran and Quan Zong took the ritual axes as left and right commanders.

sentences.zh: 會吏士疾病，故未攻而退。

translations.literal: But because officers and men fell sick, they did not attack and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Sickness swept the ranks, so they never struck and fell back.

sentences.zh: 赤烏五年，征柤中，

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chiwu he campaigned into Zuzhong,
translations.idiomatic: In Chiwu 5 (242 CE) he led a punitive expedition into the Zuzhong basin,

sentences.zh: 〈《襄阳记》曰：柤音如租税之租。

translations.literal: The Xiangyang Ji states: Zu is pronounced like the "zu" in "zu shui" (taxes).
translations.idiomatic: The Xiangyang ji notes: the graph is read like the zu in zu shui, "land tax."

sentences.zh: 柤中在上黄界，去襄阳一百五十里。

translations.literal: Zuzhong lies on the border of Shanghuang, one hundred fifty li from Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zuzhong stands on the Shanghuang frontier, a hundred and fifty li from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 魏时夷王梅敷兄弟三人，部曲万餘家屯此，分布在中庐宜城西山鄢、沔二谷中，土地平敞，宜桑麻，有水陆良田，沔南之膏腴沃壤，谓之柤中。〉

translations.literal: In Wei times the Yi king Mei Fu and his two brothers, with more than ten thousand client households, encamped there, spread between the two valleys of Yan and Mian west of the mountains in Zhonglu and Yicheng, on level ground suited to mulberry and hemp, with good farmland by water and land—the rich, irrigated soil south of the Mian, called Zuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei the Yi chieftain Mei Fu and his two brothers camped there with over ten thousand client households, straddling the Yan and Mian valleys west of the hills in Zhonglu and Yicheng—open country ideal for mulberry and hemp, laced with irrigated fields by river and road: the fat heartland south of the Mian that men call Zuzhong.

sentences.zh: 魏將蒲忠、胡質各將數千人，忠要遮險隘。

translations.literal: The Wei generals Pu Zhong and Hu Zhi each led several thousand men; Zhong blocked the defiles.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei commanders Pu Zhong and Hu Zhi each brought several thousand troops, and Pu Zhong sealed the narrow passes ahead of Zhu Ran.

sentences.zh: 圖斷然後，質為忠繼援。

translations.literal: They planned to cut off Ran from behind; Zhi acted as Zhong's follow-up support.
translations.idiomatic: They meant to sever Zhu Ran's retreat while Hu Zhi followed Pu Zhong as a second wave.

sentences.zh: 時然所督兵將先四出，聞問不暇收合，便將帳下見兵八百人逆掩。

translations.literal: At that time the officers and soldiers under Ran's command had already scattered in four directions, and before word could be gathered he led only the eight hundred men visible under his tent to meet them in a sudden strike.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ran's units were already strung out on other errands, and before he could recall them he took the eight hundred guards at headquarters and threw them straight into the ambush.

sentences.zh: 忠戰不利，質等皆退。

translations.literal: Zhong's battle went badly, and Zhi and the others all withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Zhong's attack collapsed, and Hu Zhi and the rest pulled back.

sentences.zh: 〈孙氏异同评曰：〔魏书〕及江表传云然以景初元年、正始二年再出为寇，所破胡质、蒲忠在景初元年。

translations.literal: The Sun shi yi tong ping states: The Wei shu and the Jiang Biao Zhuan say that Ran twice raided the border in the first year of Jingchu and the second year of Zhengshi, and that Hu Zhi and Pu Zhong were defeated by Ran in the first year of Jingchu.
translations.idiomatic: The Sun shi yi tong ping notes: both the Wei shu and the Jiang Biao Zhuan record Zhu Ran's two incursions in Jingchu 1 and Zhengshi 2, with Hu Zhi and Pu Zhong routed in the first Jingchu year.

sentences.zh: 魏志承魏书，依违不说质等为然所破，而直云然退耳。

translations.literal: The Wei zhi follows the Wei shu and hedges, not saying that Zhi and the others were broken by Ran, but stating flatly that Ran withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei zhi copies the Wei shu and equivocates, never admitting that Hu Zhi's men were beaten by Zhu Ran and only saying Zhu Ran retired.

sentences.zh: 吴志说赤乌五年，於魏为正始三年，魏将蒲忠与硃然战，忠不利，质等皆退。

translations.literal: The Wu zhi says that in the fifth year of Chiwu—which for Wei was the third year of Zhengshi—Wei general Pu Zhong fought Zhu Ran, Zhong fared ill, and Zhi and the others all retreated.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu zhi places the clash in Chiwu 5, which matches Wei's Zhengshi 3, and describes Wei general Pu Zhong fighting Zhu Ran to a Wei defeat followed by Hu Zhi's retreat.

sentences.zh: 按魏少帝纪及孙权传，是岁并无事，当是陈寿误以吴嘉禾六年为赤乌五年耳。〉

translations.literal: According to the annals of Wei Shao Di and Sun Quan's biography, nothing happened that year; it must be that Chen Shuo mistook Wu's sixth year of Jiahe for the fifth year of Chiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Wei annals for the young emperor and Sun Quan's memoir are silent for that year; Pei Songzhi concludes Chen Shou confused Wu's Jiahe 6 with Chiwu 5.

sentences.zh: 九年，復征柤中，魏將李興等聞然深入，率步騎六千斷然後道，然夜出逆之，軍以勝反。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he again campaigned into Zuzhong; Wei generals such as Li Xing, hearing that Ran had penetrated deep, led six thousand foot and horse to cut off Ran's rear route, but Ran issued forth by night to meet them and the army returned in victory.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he struck Zuzhong again; Li Xing and other Wei generals, learning how deep Zhu Ran had pushed, marched six thousand horse and foot to sever his line of retreat, yet Zhu Ran sallied by night, met them head-on, and marched home in triumph.

sentences.zh: 先是，歸義馬茂懷奸，覺誅，權深忿之。

translations.literal: Earlier the surrendered-in-good-faith Ma Mao had harbored treachery; when it was discovered he was executed, and Quan was deeply resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the turncoat defector Ma Mao had nursed a plot; when it was uncovered he was put to death, and Sun Quan nursed a deep grudge over the affair.

sentences.zh: 然臨行上疏曰："馬茂小子，敢負恩養。

translations.literal: As Ran was about to depart he submitted a memorial saying, "Ma Mao, that petty fellow, dared betray the favor that nurtured him.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of his expedition Zhu Ran sent up a memorial: "That wretch Ma Mao dared bite the hand that fed him.

sentences.zh: 臣今奉天威，事蒙克捷，欲令所獲，震耀遠近，方舟塞江，使足可觀，以解上下之忿。

translations.literal: Your subject now bears Heaven's majesty on the campaign; should favor grant victory, I wish to make what we capture dazzle far and near, fill the river with a fleet of boats until it is a sight worth seeing, and thereby assuage the anger above and below.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven favors this expedition I mean to parade our captives the length of the river, pack the channel with trophy ships for every eye to see, and wash away the court's fury from top to bottom.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下識臣先言，責臣後效。

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty remember your subject's earlier words and judge your subject by the outcome that follows.
translations.idiomatic: I beg only that Your Majesty recall what I have said and weigh me by the result.

sentences.zh: "權時抑表不出。

translations.literal: "At that time Quan suppressed the memorial and did not promulgate it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan pocketed the memorial and did not circulate it.

sentences.zh: 然既獻捷，群臣上賀，權乃舉酒作樂，而出然表曰："此家前初有表，孤以為難必，今果如其言，可謂明於見事也。

translations.literal: After Ran presented the spoils of victory, the host of ministers offered congratulations, and only then did Quan raise wine and set music in motion, producing Ran's memorial and saying, "This fellow submitted a memorial earlier; I thought the task beyond him, but now it has turned out exactly as he said—he may be called clear-sighted in foreseeing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ran presented his victory, the courtiers cheered, and Sun Quan at last poured the wine, called for music, and pulled out Zhu Ran's old memorial: "He warned me beforehand; I thought the thing impossible, yet it unfolded just as he promised—a man who truly reads events.

sentences.zh: "遣使拜然為左大司馬、右軍師。

translations.literal: "He sent envoys to appoint Ran as left grand marshal and right army adviser.
translations.idiomatic: He then dispatched envoys naming Zhu Ran left grand marshal and right army adviser.

sentences.zh: 然長不盈七尺，氣候分明。

translations.literal: Ran was not quite seven chi in height, yet his bearing was distinct and clear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ran stood under seven chi, but his presence was unmistakable.

sentences.zh: 內行修潔，其所文采，惟施軍器，余皆質素。

translations.literal: His private conduct was disciplined and clean; whatever ornament he allowed himself he applied only to military gear, and everything else was plain.
translations.idiomatic: In private life he was austere: color and polish went only to weapons and armor; the rest of his wardrobe stayed plain.

sentences.zh: 終日欽欽，常在戰場，臨急膽定。

translations.literal: All day long he was intent and alert, constantly on the battlefield; faced with crisis his courage steadied.
translations.idiomatic: He remained intent from dawn to dusk, lived on campaign, and in crisis his nerve never wavered.

sentences.zh: 尤過絕人。

translations.literal: In this he surpassed others utterly.
translations.idiomatic: In that calm courage he stood above ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 雖世無事，每朝夕嚴鼓，兵在營者，鹹行裝就隊。

translations.literal: Even when the age was without incident, morning and evening he beat the war drum with severity; soldiers in camp all donned kit and fell into formation.
translations.idiomatic: Even in peacetime he beat the morning and evening drums without fail, and every man under canvas belted on gear and stood to ranks.

sentences.zh: 以此玩敵，使不知所備，故出輒有功。

translations.literal: By this means he toyed with the enemy and left them unsure what to prepare for, so that whenever he went forth he invariably had success.
translations.idiomatic: He habitually wrong-footed the foe so they never knew what to expect, and his outings therefore seldom failed.

sentences.zh: 諸葛瑾子融，步騭子協，雖各襲任，權特復使然總為大督。

translations.literal: Though the sons of Zhuge Jin, Rong, and of Bu Zhi, Xie, each inherited their fathers' posts, Quan specially had Ran again act as supreme commander over all.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhuge Jin's son Zhuge Rong and Bu Zhi's son Bu Xie had each stepped into their fathers' shoes, Sun Quan still named Zhu Ran overall commander above them.

sentences.zh: 又陸遜亦本，功臣名將存者惟然，莫與比隆。

translations.literal: Moreover Lu Xun had also died; of the founding meritorious generals who survived there was only Ran—none could compare with him in eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun was gone as well; among the old guard still alive only Zhu Ran remained, and none matched his stature.

sentences.zh: 寢疾二年，後漸增篤，權晝為減膳。

translations.literal: He lay ill two years; later his condition gradually grew grave, and Quan by day reduced his meals for him.
translations.idiomatic: For two years he lingered bedridden, then sank visibly; Sun Quan cut his own daytime meals out of grief for him.

sentences.zh: 夜為不寐，中使醫藥口食之物，相望於道。

translations.literal: By night he could not sleep; palace messengers with medicines and mouth-fed foods crowded the road.
translations.idiomatic: At night he could not sleep, and imperial couriers bearing drugs and broth clogged the road to Zhu Ran's house.

sentences.zh: 然每遣使表疾病消息，權輒召見，口自問訊。

translations.literal: Whenever Ran sent messengers to memorialize the news of his illness, Quan would always summon them for audience and personally inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Each time Zhu Ran's couriers arrived with word of his health, Sun Quan received them in person and asked after Zhu Ran himself.

sentences.zh: 入賜酒食，出送布帛。

translations.literal: When they entered he granted wine and food; when they departed he sent them off with cloth and silk.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted them on entry and pressed silks on them when they left.

sentences.zh: 自創業功臣疾病，權意之所鐘，呂蒙、淩統最重，然其次矣。

translations.literal: Among the founding meritors who fell sick, those whom Quan's heart favored most were Lü Meng and Ling Tong, with Ran next after them.
translations.idiomatic: Of the founders who sickened, Sun Quan grieved deepest for Lü Meng and Ling Tong; Zhu Ran came just after those two.

sentences.zh: 年六十八，赤烏十二年卒，權素服舉哀，為之感慟。

translations.literal: In his sixty-eighth year he died in the twelfth year of Chiwu; Quan wore unbleached mourning and conducted lamentation for him, moved to tears for his sake.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-eight in Chiwu 12; Sun Quan donned white mourning, held a state lament, and wept for him.

sentences.zh: 子績嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ji succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu Ji inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 子 施績

translations.literal: Son: Shi Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was his son, known as Shi Ji before the surname was restored.

sentences.zh: 績字公緒，以父任為郎，後拜建忠都尉。

translations.literal: Ji, courtesy name Gongxu, by his father's position became a gentleman, and later was appointed commandant who establishes loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ji, styled Gongxu, entered the court as a gentleman through his father's rank, then received appointment as commandant who establishes loyalty.

sentences.zh: 叔父才卒，績領其兵，隨太常潘浚討五溪，以膽力稱。

translations.literal: When his uncle Cai died, Ji took over his troops, followed the chamberlain Pan Jun in the campaign against the Five Gorges tribes, and was famed for courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: When his uncle Zhu Cai died, Zhu Ji inherited his command, followed the chamberlain Pan Jun against the Five Gorges tribes, and won a name for raw nerve.

sentences.zh: 遷偏將軍營下督，領盜賊事，持法不傾。

translations.literal: He was promoted to lieutenant general and camp superintendent, in charge of bandit affairs, and upheld the law without partiality.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to lieutenant general and camp superintendent with charge of bandit suppression, enforcing the code without bending.

sentences.zh: 魯王霸注意交績，嘗至其廨，就之坐，欲與結好，績下地住立，辭而不當。

translations.literal: The prince of Lu, Ba, paid court to Ji, once coming to his office, taking a seat beside him, and wishing to strike up friendship; Ji stepped down to the floor and stood, declining and refusing the honor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sun Ba of Lu cultivated him, even visiting his yamen, sitting down at his side, and offering friendship; Zhu Ji rose, stood on the floor, and refused the overture as improper.

sentences.zh: 然卒。

translations.literal: Ran died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ran died.

sentences.zh: 績襲業，拜平魏將軍，樂鄉督。

translations.literal: Ji inherited the enterprise and was appointed general who pacifies Wei and commander at Lexiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ji took up his father's post as general who pacifies Wei and garrison commander at Lexiang.

sentences.zh: 明年，魏徵南將軍王昶率眾攻江陵城，不克而退。

translations.literal: The next year Wei's general who campaigns south, Wang Chang, led a host against Jiangling city but could not take it and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wang Chang, Wei's general who campaigns south, stormed Jiangling without success and retired.

sentences.zh: 績與奮威將軍諸葛融書曰："昶遠來疲睏，馬無所食，力屈而走，此天助也。

translations.literal: Ji wrote to the fierce tiger general Zhuge Rong, saying, "Chang has come from afar weary and famished; his horses have nothing to eat, and his strength failed so he fled—this is Heaven aiding us.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ji wrote to Zhuge Rong, the fierce tiger general: "Wang Chang marched here spent and starving, his horses found no fodder, and he broke off from sheer exhaustion—that is Heaven fighting on our side.

sentences.zh: 今追之力少，可引兵相繼，吾欲破之於前，足下乘之於後，豈一人之功哉，宜同斷金之義。

translations.literal: Now the force that pursues him is small; you can bring up troops in succession. I wish to shatter him in the van while you ride him down from the rear—how could the credit be one man's alone? We ought to share the resolve of men who would cleave metal together.
translations.idiomatic: Our pursuit column is thin; feed in reinforcements behind me. I will break him from the front while you hammer him from the rear—the glory cannot be one man's; we should cleave one purpose like brothers sworn to split metal.

sentences.zh: "融答許績。

translations.literal: "Rong answered agreeing to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Rong wrote back promising to join him.

sentences.zh: 績便引兵及昶於紀南，紀南去城三十里，績先戰勝而融不進，績後失利。

translations.literal: Ji thereupon led troops and overtook Chang at Jinan; Jinan was thirty li from the city, Ji first fought and won but Rong did not advance, and afterward Ji suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ji marched and caught Wang Chang at Jinan, thirty li from the walls; Zhu Ji opened with a victory but Zhuge Rong never moved up, and Zhu Ji later lost the field.

sentences.zh: 權深嘉績，盛責怒融，融兄大將軍恪貴重，故融得不廢。

translations.literal: Quan deeply praised Ji and fiercely rebuked Rong; yet because Rong's elder brother the grand general Ke was so powerful, Rong was not dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan heaped praise on Zhu Ji and blistered Zhuge Rong, yet spared Rong because his brother Zhuge Ke still towered at court.

sentences.zh: 初績與恪、融不平，及此事變，為隙益甚。

translations.literal: At first Ji had been on bad terms with Ke and Rong, and after this incident the rift grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ji had long distrusted Zhuge Ke and Zhuge Rong; after that battle the bad blood only deepened.

sentences.zh: 建興元年，遷鎮東將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianxing he was promoted to general who guards the east.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 1 he advanced to general who guards the east.

sentences.zh: 二年春，恪向新城，要績並力，而留置半州，使融兼其任。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year Ke advanced on Xincheng and summoned Ji to join forces with him, but instead detained him at Banzhou and had Rong take over his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Next spring Zhuge Ke marched on Xincheng and called for Zhu Ji's weight in the line, yet kept him half-stranded at Banzhou while Zhuge Rong doubled his jobs.

sentences.zh: 冬，恪、融被害，績復還樂鄉，假節。

translations.literal: In winter Ke and Rong were killed; Ji returned to Lexiang and was given the baton of office.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zhuge Ke and Zhuge Rong perished; Zhu Ji went back to Lexiang with credentials as commander.

sentences.zh: 太平二年，拜驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping he was appointed chief of cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping 2 he was named chief of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 孫綝秉政，大臣疑貳，績恐吳必擾亂，而中國乘釁，乃密書結蜀，使為並兼之慮。

translations.literal: When Sun Lin seized power the great ministers wavered; Ji feared that Wu would surely fall into turmoil while the Central Plains exploited the breach, and therefore secretly wrote to Shu asking them to plan for a joint strike.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sun Lin dominated the court and high officials eyed one another with suspicion, Zhu Ji feared Wu would tear apart while the north rushed through the gap, and he secretly wrote to Shu urging coordinated contingency plans.

sentences.zh: 蜀遣右將軍閻宇將兵五千，增白帝守，以須績之後命。

translations.literal: Shu dispatched the right general Yan Yu with five thousand troops to reinforce the defense of Baidi and await Ji's further orders.
translations.idiomatic: Shu answered by sending the right general Yan Yu with five thousand men to stiffen Baidi's garrison pending Zhu Ji's signal.

sentences.zh: 永安初，遷上大將軍、都護督，自巴丘上迄西陵，元興元年，就拜左大司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongan he was promoted to supreme grand general and commander-in-chief; from Baqiu upstream to Xiling fell under his charge, and in the first year of Yuanxing he received appointment as left grand marshal on site.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongan he rose to supreme grand general and commander-in-chief from Baqiu upriver to Xiling, and in Yuanxing 1 took the left grand marshal's seal where he stood.

sentences.zh: 初，然為治行喪竟，乞復本姓，權不許，績以五鳳中表還為施氏，建衡二年卒。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ran had finished mourning for Zhi, he begged to resume his original surname, but Quan did not permit it; in the Wufeng era Ji memorialized to revert to the Shi surname, and he died in the second year of Jianheng.
translations.idiomatic: Years before, after Zhu Ran had mourned Zhu Zhi, he asked to take back the Shi surname, but Sun Quan refused; in the Wufeng era Zhu Ji petitioned again for the Shi name, and he died in Jianheng 2.

sentences.zh: 呂范字子衡，汝南細陽人也。

translations.literal: Lü Fan, courtesy name Ziheng, was a native of Xiyang in Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Fan, styled Ziheng, came from Xiyang in Runan commandery.

sentences.zh: 少為縣吏，有容觀姿貌。

translations.literal: In youth he was a county clerk and had a handsome bearing and comely appearance.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he served as a county clerk and cut a striking figure.

sentences.zh: 邑人劉氏，家富女美，范求之。

translations.literal: A man of his township surnamed Liu had a rich household and a beautiful daughter, and Fan sought her in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: A local magnate surnamed Liu had wealth and a lovely daughter; Lü Fan asked for her hand.

sentences.zh: 女母嫌，欲勿與，劉氏曰："觀呂子衡，寧當久貧者邪?"遂與之婚。

translations.literal: The girl's mother disliked him and wished not to give her, but the Liu said, "Look at Lü Ziheng—could he long remain poor?" and thus gave her in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The mother balked, but the father said, "Look at Lü Ziheng—do you think he will stay poor forever?" and the match was made.

sentences.zh: 後避亂壽春，孫策見而異之，范遂自委暱，將私客百人歸策。

translations.literal: Later, fleeing turmoil, he went to Shouchun; Sun Ce saw him and marveled at him, whereupon Fan attached himself in intimacy, leading a hundred private retainers to join Ce.
translations.idiomatic: He later fled the wars to Shouchun; Sun Ce singled him out at sight, and Lü Fan pledged himself, bringing a hundred household warriors into Sun Ce's camp.

sentences.zh: 時太妃在江都，策遣范迎之。

translations.literal: At that time the grand consort was at Jiangdu, and Ce sent Fan to welcome her.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady Dowager was still at Jiangdu, and Sun Ce sent Lü Fan to escort her.

sentences.zh: 徐州牧陶謙謂范為袁氏覘候，諷縣掠考范，范親客健兒篡取以歸。

translations.literal: The provincial governor of Xu Province, Tao Qian, thought Fan was spying for the Yuans and hinted to the county to seize and torture Fan; Fan's trusted fighting men snatched him back and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qian, governor of Xu Province, took Lü Fan for a Yuan spy and had the county jail him for questioning; Lü Fan's stalwart retainers broke him out and carried him home.

sentences.zh: 時唯范與孫河常從策，跨涉辛苦，危難不避，策亦親戚待之，每與升堂飲宴於太妃前。

translations.literal: At that time only Fan and Sun He constantly followed Ce, crossing hardships and dangers without shunning them, and Ce also treated them as kin, ascending the hall with them to drink and feast before the grand consort.
translations.idiomatic: Only Lü Fan and Sun He stayed constantly at Sun Ce's side through every hardship; Sun Ce treated them like family and brought them to the inner hall to feast before his mother.

sentences.zh: 後從策攻破廬江，還俱東渡，到橫江、當利，破長英、於麋，下小丹楊、湖孰，領湖孰相。

translations.literal: Later he followed Ce in storming Lujiang, and both went east across the river, reaching Hengjiang and Dangli, defeating Zhang Ying and Yu Mi, taking Lesser Danyang and Hushu, and Fan was given charge as chancellor of Hushu.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Sun Ce's storming of Lujiang, crossed east with him to Hengjiang and Dangli, broke Zhang Ying and Yu Mi, took Lesser Danyang and Hushu, and Lü Fan became chancellor of Hushu.

sentences.zh: 策定秣陵、曲阿，收笮融，劉繇餘眾，增范兵二千，騎五十匹。

translations.literal: After Ce pacified Moling and Qu'e, gathered Ze Rong and Liu Yao's remaining troops, he increased Fan's soldiers by two thousand and gave him fifty horses.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sun Ce secured Moling and Qu'e, absorbed Ze Rong and Liu Yao's remnants, he added two thousand foot and fifty horses to Lü Fan's command.

sentences.zh: 後領宛陵令，討破丹楊賊，還吳，遷都督。

translations.literal: Later he held the magistracy of Wanling, attacked and defeated the bandits of Danyang, returned to Wu, and was promoted to area commander.
translations.idiomatic: He later governed Wanling, crushed the Danyang bandits, came back to Wu, and rose to area commander.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：策从容独与范釭，范曰：“今将军事业日大，士众日盛，范在远，闻纲纪犹有不整者，范原蹔领都督，佐将军部分之。

translations.literal: The Jiang Biao Zhuan states: Ce at ease was alone with Fan playing pitch-pot, and Fan said, "Now the general's enterprise grows daily and your host increases daily; though Fan is far away I hear that discipline is still not entirely in order; Fan wishes temporarily to take the post of area commander to assist the general in assigning duties.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang Biao Zhuan records a pitch-pot game alone with Sun Ce: Lü Fan said, "Your enterprise swells by the day and so does your army; even from afar I hear the staff is not fully knit; let me hold the area commander's seal for a time and help you sort the ranks.

sentences.zh: ”策曰：“子衡，卿既士大夫，加手下已有大众，立功於外，岂宜复屈小职，知军中细碎事乎！

translations.literal: "Ce said, "Ziheng, you are already a gentleman-official, and moreover under your hand you already have a great host and have won merit in the field—how should you again humble yourself to a petty post and know the petty affairs of the army!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce answered, "Ziheng, you are a man of standing with a large following and battlefield laurels—why demean yourself to clerk's work inside camp?

sentences.zh: ”范曰：“不然。

translations.literal: "Fan said, "It is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Fan replied, "That is not the point.

sentences.zh: 今舍本土而讬将军者，非为妻子也，欲济世务。

translations.literal: Now those who have left their native soil and entrusted themselves to the general do not do it for wives and children; they wish to rescue the affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Those who left home to follow you are not here for wives and children; they mean to set the age to rights.

sentences.zh: 犹同舟涉海，一事不牢，即俱受其败。

translations.literal: It is like sharing one boat to cross the sea—if one thing is not secure, all alike suffer the wreck.
translations.idiomatic: We share one boat on a wide sea: one loose rope drowns everyone aboard.

sentences.zh: 此亦范计，非但将军也。

translations.literal: This too is Fan's plan, not for the general alone.
translations.idiomatic: This is my calculus too, not only yours.

sentences.zh: ”策笑，无以答。

translations.literal: "Ce laughed and had no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce laughed and had no answer.

sentences.zh: 范出，更释褠，著袴褶，执鞭，诣閤下启事，自称领都督，策乃授传，委以众事。

translations.literal: Fan went out, changed from his jacket-skirt into riding coat and trousers, took a whip, went to the headquarters gate to report business, and styled himself acting area commander, whereupon Ce handed him the tally and entrusted him with the host of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Fan left, swapped his gown for field dress, took a riding crop, presented himself at headquarters as acting area commander, and Sun Ce gave him the tally and the whole staff.

sentences.zh: 由是军中肃睦，威禁大行。〉

translations.literal: From this the army was solemn and harmonious, and awe-inspiring prohibitions were widely enforced.
translations.idiomatic: After that the host grew orderly, and stern regulations ran through every camp.

sentences.zh: 是時下邳陳瑀自號吳都太守，住海西，與強族嚴白虎交通。

translations.literal: At that time Chen Yu of Xiapi styled himself grand administrator of Wu and stayed at Haixi, communicating with the powerful clan Yan Baihu.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Chen Yu of Xiapi called himself governor of Wu, held Haixi, and dealt with the magnate Yan Baihu.

sentences.zh: 策自將討虎，別遣范與徐逸攻瑀於海西，梟其大將陳牧。

translations.literal: Ce personally led the host to attack Hu, separately sending Fan with Xu Yi to attack Yu at Haixi, and beheading Yu's great general Chen Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce marched in person against Yan Baihu while detaching Lü Fan and Xu Yi to strike Chen Yu at Haixi, taking the head of Chen Yu's champion Chen Mu.

sentences.zh: 〈《九州春秋》曰：初平三年，扬州刺史陈祎死，袁术使瑀领扬州牧。

translations.literal: The Jiu zhou chun qiu states: In the third year of Chuping the Yangzhou inspector Chen Yi died, and Yuan Shu had Yu take charge as shepherd of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiu zhou chun qiu says: in Chuping 3 the Yangzhou inspector Chen Yi died and Yuan Shu named Chen Yu acting shepherd of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 后术为曹公所败於封丘，南人叛瑀，瑀拒之。

translations.literal: Later Shu was defeated by Lord Cao at Fengqiu, and the southerners rebelled against Yu, but Yu resisted them.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuan Shu lost to Cao Cao at Fengqiu; the south turned on Chen Yu, and Chen Yu held the line against them.

sentences.zh: 术走阴陵，好辞以下瑀，瑀不知权，而又怯，不即攻术。

translations.literal: Shu fled to Yinling and used fine words to humble himself before Yu, but Yu did not grasp the moment and, being timid, did not immediately attack Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu fled to Yinling with smooth talk and humble phrases, yet Chen Yu misread the moment and, out of timidity, never struck while the chance lasted.

sentences.zh: 术於淮北集兵向寿春。

translations.literal: Shu thereupon gathered troops north of the Huai and aimed at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu then massed troops north of the Huai and marched on Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 瑀惧，使其弟公琰请和於术。

translations.literal: Yu was afraid and sent his younger brother Gongyan to sue for peace with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu panicked and sent his brother Chen Gongyan to beg a truce of Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 术执之而进，瑀走归下邳。〉

translations.literal: Shu seized him and advanced; Yu fled back to Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu seized the envoy and pressed forward, and Chen Yu bolted home to Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 又從攻祖郎於陵陽，太史慈於勇裡。

translations.literal: He also followed in attacking Zu Lang at Lingyang and Tai Shi Ci at Yongli.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined the attacks on Zu Lang at Lingyang and Tai Shi Ci at Yongli.

sentences.zh: 七縣平定，拜征虜中郎將，征江夏，還平鄱陽。

translations.literal: Seven counties were pacified, and he was appointed general of the household who campaigns against captives, campaigned against Jiangxia, returned, and pacified Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Seven counties were settled; Lü Fan became general of the household who campaigns against captives, struck Jiangxia, then swung back to quiet Poyang.

sentences.zh: 策薨，奔喪於吳。

translations.literal: When Ce died, he rushed to Wu for the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce died he raced to Wu for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 後權復征江夏，范與張昭留守。

translations.literal: Later, when Quan again campaigned against Jiangxia, Fan stayed behind with Zhang Zhao as guard.
translations.idiomatic: Later Sun Quan renewed the Jiangxia campaign and left Lü Fan with Zhang Zhao to hold the rear.

sentences.zh: 曹公至赤壁，與周瑜等俱拒破之，拜裨將軍，領彭澤太守，以彭澤、柴桑、歷陽為奉邑。

translations.literal: When Lord Cao reached Chibi, together with Zhou Yu and the others he resisted and defeated him, and Fan was appointed lieutenant general, given the magistracy of Pengze, and granted Pengze, Chaisang, and Liyang as his support fief.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao came to Chibi, Lü Fan stood with Zhou Yu and broke him; Lü Fan was named lieutenant general, governor of Pengze, and given Pengze, Chaisang, and Liyang as fiscal domain.

sentences.zh: 劉備詣京見權，范密請留備。

translations.literal: Liu Bei went to the capital to see Quan, and Fan secretly asked that Bei be detained.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei visited Jing to meet Sun Quan, Lü Fan privately urged Sun Quan to hold him fast.

sentences.zh: 後遷平南將軍，屯柴桑。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to general who pacifies the south and garrisoned Chaisang.
translations.idiomatic: He was later raised to general who pacifies the south and camped at Chaisang.

sentences.zh: 權討關羽，過范館。

translations.literal: When Quan campaigned against Guan Yu, he passed Fan's lodge.
translations.idiomatic: On Sun Quan's expedition against Guan Yu he stopped at Lü Fan's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 謂曰："昔早從卿言，無此勞也。

translations.literal: He said to him, "If long ago I had followed your advice, I would not have this toil now.
translations.idiomatic: He told him, "Had I listened to you sooner, I would be spared this grind.

sentences.zh: 今當上取之，卿為我守建業。

translations.literal: Now I am about to go up and take him; you shall guard Jianye for me.
translations.idiomatic: I go north to take him; you will hold Jianye for me.

sentences.zh: "權破羽還，都武昌，拜范建威將軍，封宛陵候，領丹楊太守，治建業，督扶州以下至海，轉以溧陽、懷安、寧國為奉邑。

translations.literal: "After Quan broke Yu and returned, he established his capital at Wuchang, appointed Fan general who establishes might, enfeoffed him as marquis of Wanling, gave him the magistracy of Danyang with administration at Jianye, and charged him from Fuzhou down to the sea, then shifted his support fief to Liyang, Huai'an, and Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Quan crushed Guan Yu he moved the court to Wuchang, made Lü Fan general who establishes might, marquis of Wanling, governor of Danyang administering from Jianye, with command from Fuzhou to the sea, and later shifted his stipend towns to Liyang, Huai'an, and Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 曹休、張遼，臧霸等來伐，范督徐盛、全琮、孫韶等，以舟師拒休等於洞口。

translations.literal: Cao Xiu, Zhang Liao, Zang Ba, and others came to attack, and Fan directed Xu Sheng, Quan Zong, Sun Shao, and others, meeting Xiu and the others at Dongkou with the fleet.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiu, Zhang Liao, Zang Ba, and others invaded Wu; Lü Fan led Xu Sheng, Quan Zong, Sun Shao, and the river fleet against Cao Xiu at Dongkou.

sentences.zh: 遷前將軍，假節，改封南昌候。

translations.literal: He was promoted to forward general, lent the baton of office, and his fief was changed to marquis of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to forward general, took the baton, and traded his fief for the marquisate of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 時遭大風，船人覆溺，死者數千，還軍，拜揚州牧。

translations.literal: At that time they encountered a great wind; men of the boats capsized and drowned, and those who died numbered in the thousands; returning the army, he was appointed shepherd of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A gale caught the fleet; thousands drowned when boats rolled; on the withdrawal he was named shepherd of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 性好威儀，州民如陸遜、全琮及貴公子，皆修敬虔肅，不敢輕脫。

translations.literal: His nature loved imposing ceremony; commoners of the province such as Lu Xun and Quan Zong, as well as noble sons, all cultivated respect and solemnity and did not dare behave lightly.
translations.idiomatic: He loved pomp: even great men like Lu Xun and Quan Zong, to say nothing of younger lords, approached him with stiff formality.

sentences.zh: 其居處服飾，於時奢靡，然勤事奉法，故權悅其忠，不怪其侈。

translations.literal: His dwelling and dress were extravagant for the time, yet he was diligent in affairs and observed the law, so Quan was pleased with his loyalty and did not blame his luxury.
translations.idiomatic: His house and wardrobe ran to splendor, yet he toiled at duty and kept the code, so Sun Quan prized his loyalty and forgave the flash.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：人有白范与贺齐奢丽夸绮，服饰僭拟王者，权曰：“昔管仲逾礼，桓公优而容之，无损於霸。

translations.literal: The Jiang Biao Zhuan states: Someone reported that Fan and He Qi were extravagantly splendid and that their dress aped the king's; Quan said, "In old days Guan Zhong exceeded ritual, yet Duke Huan indulged him without harm to hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang Biao Zhuan says informers charged Lü Fan and He Qi with finery fit for a king; Sun Quan replied, "Guan Zhong once overstepped rites, yet Duke Huan smiled and bore it without losing the hegemony.

sentences.zh: 今子衡、公苗，身无夷吾之失，但其器械精好，舟车严整耳，此適足作军容，何损於治哉？

translations.literal: Now Ziheng and Gongmiao have none of Guan Zhong's faults, only that their gear is fine and their chariots and boats trim—this is precisely what adorns a host; how does it injure governance?
translations.idiomatic: Ziheng and Gongmiao commit none of Guan Zhong's sins; their gear is simply polished and their convoys smart—that only dresses the army; what harm is there to rule?

sentences.zh: ”告者乃不敢复言。〉

translations.literal: "The informer then did not dare speak again.
translations.idiomatic: The accuser never dared raise the matter again.

sentences.zh: 初策使范曲主財計，權時年少，私從有求，范必關白，不敢專許，當時以此見望。

translations.literal: At first Ce had Fan take charge of accounts at Qu; Quan was then young and privately made requests of Fan, but Fan invariably reported them and did not dare consent on his own authority, and for this reason was at the time resented.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce had put Lü Fan in charge of the books at Qu; young Sun Quan would dip into the funds for private ends, yet Lü Fan always reported each request upward and never signed off alone—so the heir once thought him tiresome.

sentences.zh: 權守陽羨長，有所私用，策或料覆，功曹周谷輒為傅著薄書，使無譴問。

translations.literal: When Quan was guarding Yangxian as magistrate and had private expenditures, Ce sometimes audited the accounts, and the merit officer Zhou Gu would then forge ledger entries so that there would be no reproach or inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan governed Yangxian and skimmed the ledgers, Sun Ce sometimes audited the books; merit officer Zhou Gu would falsify the registers so no questions followed.

sentences.zh: 權臨時悅之，及後統事，以范忠誠，厚見信任，以谷能欺更簿書，不用也。

translations.literal: Quan at the time was pleased with him, but after he later took charge of affairs, because Fan was loyal and honest he trusted him deeply, and because Gu could deceive and alter the ledgers, he did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan had liked Zhou Gu in the moment, but once he ruled the realm he prized Lü Fan's honesty and relied on him heavily, while Zhou Gu, who knew only how to cook books, never won office again.

sentences.zh: 黃武七年，范遷大司馬，印綬未下，疾卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Huangwu Fan was promoted to grand marshal, but before the seal and ribbon were issued he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangwu 7 Lü Fan was named grand marshal; the credentials never reached him—he died first.

sentences.zh: 權素服舉哀，遣使者追贈印綬。

translations.literal: Quan wore unbleached mourning and conducted lamentation for him, sending envoys to posthumously bestow the seal and ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan wore white, held a state lament, and sent envoys to confer the seal and ribbon after his death.

sentences.zh: 及還都建業，權過范墓呼曰："子衡!"言及流涕，祀以太牢。

translations.literal: When he returned the capital to Jianye, Quan passed Fan's tomb and called out, "Ziheng!" spoke to the point of shedding tears, and sacrificed with the grand ox.
translations.idiomatic: After moving the court to Jianye he stopped at Lü Fan's grave, cried "Ziheng!" until tears ran, and offered the highest sacrifice of an ox.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：初，权移都建业，大会将相文武，时谓严畯曰：“孤昔叹鲁子敬比邓禹，吕子衡方吴汉，间卿诸人未平此论，今定云何？

translations.literal: The Jiang Biao Zhuan states: At first, when Quan moved the capital to Jianye, he held a great assembly of civil and military ministers, and at the time said to Yan Jun, "Long ago I sighed that Lu Zijing might be compared to Deng Yu and Lü Ziheng to Wu Han; meanwhile you gentlemen have not accepted that judgment—what do you say now that things are settled?
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang Biao Zhuan says: when Sun Quan first shifted the seat to Jianye he feasted his commanders and asked Yan Jun, "I once ranked Lu Su with Deng Yu and Lü Fan with Wu Han, and you all demurred—now that time has tested them, what is your verdict?

sentences.zh: ”畯退席曰：“臣未解指趣，谓肃、范受饶，褒叹过实。

translations.literal: "Jun left his mat and said, "Your subject did not grasp the point and thought that Su and Fan had received excessive praise and that the praise overshot the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun rose from his cushion and said, "I failed to see your meaning and assumed Your Majesty had overstated Lu Su and Lü Fan.

sentences.zh: ”权曰：“昔邓仲华初见光武，光武时受更始使，抚河北，行大司马事耳，未有帝王志也。

translations.literal: "Quan said, "In old days Deng Zhonghua first met Guangwu; Guangwu at the time was on an errand for the Gengshi Emperor, pacifying the north of the Yellow River, and merely acted as grand marshal—he had not yet the mind of an emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan answered, "When Deng Yu first met Guangwu, the emperor was still an envoy of Gengshi pacifying Hebei and holding only the grand marshal's baton—no imperial ambition yet.

sentences.zh: 禹劝之以复汉业，是禹开初议之端矣。

translations.literal: Yu urged him to restore the house of Han, and thus Yu opened the beginning of the first counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yu pressed him to revive the Han; he opened the first serious counsel.

sentences.zh: 子敬英爽有殊略，孤始与一语，便及大计，与禹相似，故比之。

translations.literal: Zijing is heroic and keen and has an extraordinary plan; the first time I spoke with him alone he came to the great design—he resembles Yu, and therefore I compared him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su is bold and far-sighted; one private word with me touched the grand strategy—like Deng Yu, hence the parallel.

sentences.zh: 吕子衡忠笃亮直，性虽好奢，然以忧公为先，不足为损，避袁术自归於兄，兄作大将，别领部曲，故忧兄事，乞为都督，办护脩整，加之恪勤，与吴汉相类，故方之。

translations.literal: Lü Ziheng is loyal, staunch, and upright; though his nature loves luxury, he put worry for the public first, which is not enough to count as harm; fleeing Yuan Shu he attached himself to his elder brother, and when his elder brother became a great general and separately led a host, therefore worrying over his elder brother's affairs, he begged to be area commander to put the host in order and repair discipline, and added to that diligent care—he resembles Wu Han, and therefore I paired him with Wu Han.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Fan fled Yuan Shu to my brother, served my brother's separate command, begged the area command to set the army in order, and though fond of display always put the state first—Wu Han in another skin, so I named him thus.

sentences.zh: 皆有指趣，非孤私之也。

translations.literal: In each case there was a point; it was not my private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Each comparison had a point; it was no private favor.

sentences.zh: ”畯乃服。〉

translations.literal: "Only then did Jun submit.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun conceded.

sentences.zh: 范長子先卒，次子據嗣。

translations.literal: Fan's eldest son died earlier; the second son Ju inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Fan's eldest son died young; the second son Lü Ju succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 子 據

translations.literal: Son: Ju.
translations.idiomatic: The heir: Lü Ju.

sentences.zh: 據字世議。

translations.literal: Ju, courtesy name Shiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Ju, styled Shiyi.

sentences.zh: 以父任為郎，後范寢疾，拜副軍校尉，佐領軍事。

translations.literal: By his father's position he became a gentleman; later, when Fan lay gravely ill, he was appointed deputy colonel of the army and assisted in directing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's rank he entered as a gentleman; when Lü Fan fell mortally ill he became deputy colonel of the army and helped run the staff.

sentences.zh: 范卒，遷安軍中郎將。

translations.literal: When Fan died, he was promoted to gentleman of the household for the stabilization of the army.
translations.idiomatic: After Lü Fan died he was promoted to gentleman of the household attached to the army stabilization command.

sentences.zh: 數討山賊，諸深惡劇地，所擊皆破、隨太常潘浚討五溪，復有功。

translations.literal: He repeatedly campaigned against mountain bandits; in every deeply treacherous and harsh place where he struck, he broke them; following the chamberlain Pan Jun against the Five Gorges tribes, he again had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly cleared mountain strongholds in the worst terrain and never failed; he followed Pan Jun against the Five Gorges and won further distinction.

sentences.zh: 朱然攻樊，據與朱異破城外圍，還拜偏將軍。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ran attacked Fancheng, Ju together with Zhu Yi broke the outer stockade outside the walls, and on return he was appointed lieutenant general.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ran besieged Fancheng, Lü Ju and Zhu Yi tore down the outer ring of fortifications, and Lü Ju came home a lieutenant general.

sentences.zh: 入補馬閒右部督，遷越騎校尉。

translations.literal: He entered to fill the post of commander of the right section of the horse corral and was promoted to colonel of the agile cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was called in as commander of the right wing of the horse corral, then promoted to colonel of the agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 太元元年，大風，江水溢流，漸淹城門，權使視水，獨見據使人取大船以備害。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiyuan a great wind blew, the Yangtze overflowed, and gradually flooded the city gates; Quan sent men to inspect the waters and alone saw Ju dispatch men to fetch great ships against the harm.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiyuan 1 a gale drove the river over its banks toward the gates; Sun Quan's inspectors found only Lü Ju launching great ships to meet the flood.

sentences.zh: 權嘉之，拜蕩魏將軍。

translations.literal: Quan praised him and appointed him general who smashes Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan commended him and named him general who smashes Wei.

sentences.zh: 權寢疾，以據為太子右部督。

translations.literal: When Quan lay gravely ill, he made Ju commander of the crown prince's right section.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan fell seriously ill he named Lü Ju commander of the heir apparent's right guard.

sentences.zh: 太子即位，拜右將軍。

translations.literal: When the crown prince ascended the throne, he was appointed right general.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince succeeded, Lü Ju became right general.

sentences.zh: 魏出東興，據赴討有功。

translations.literal: When Wei came out against Dongxing, Ju hurried to the attack and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei struck Dongxing, Lü Ju marched to the relief and earned credit.

sentences.zh: 明年，孫峻殺諸葛恪，遷據為驃騎將軍，平西宮事。

translations.literal: The next year Sun Jun killed Zhuge Ke and promoted Ju to chief of cavalry with charge of the western palace.
