translations.idiomatic: The next year Sun Jun murdered Zhuge Ke and advanced Lü Ju to chief of cavalry with custody of the western palace.

sentences.zh: 五鳳二年，假節，與峻等襲壽春，還遇魏將曹珍，破之於高亭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wufeng he was lent the baton of office and with Jun and others raided Shouchun; on the return he met Wei general Cao Zhen and defeated him at Gaoting.
translations.idiomatic: In Wufeng 2 he took the baton, joined Sun Jun's raid on Shouchun, and on the way back smashed Cao Zhen at Gaoting.

sentences.zh: 太平元年，帥師侵魏，未及淮，聞孫峻死，以從弟綝自代，據大怒，引軍還，欲廢綝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiping he led the army to invade Wei; before reaching the Huai he heard that Sun Jun had died and that his cousin Lin had replaced himself; Ju was greatly angry, led the army back, and wished to depose Lin.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping 1 he invaded Wei but turned back short of the Huai when he learned Sun Jun was dead and Sun Lin had seized power; enraged, he marched home intending to depose Sun Lin.

sentences.zh: 綝聞之，使中書奉詔，詔文欽、劉纂，唐咨等使取據，又遣從兄慮以都下兵逆據於江都。

translations.literal: When Lin heard of it, he had the secretariat present an edict ordering Wen Qin, Liu Zuan, Tang Zi, and others to seize Ju, and also sent his cousin Lu with capital troops to intercept Ju at Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin answered with an edict through the secretariat, ordering Wen Qin, Liu Zuan, and Tang Zi to arrest Lü Ju while his cousin Sun Lu blocked him at Jiangdu with the capital garrison.

sentences.zh: 左右勸據降魏，據曰："恥為叛臣。

translations.literal: Those at his side urged Ju to surrender to Wei; Ju said, "It would shame me to be a traitor minister.
translations.idiomatic: His staff urged defection to Wei; Lü Ju said, "I will not live as a turncoat.

sentences.zh: "遂自殺。

translations.literal: "Thereupon he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: He then took his own life.

sentences.zh: 夷三族。

translations.literal: Three degrees of kin were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: His kin to the third degree were extirpated.

sentences.zh: 朱桓字休穆，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Huan, courtesy name Xiumu, was a native of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Huan, styled Xiumu, came from Wu in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 孫權為將軍，桓給事幕府，除餘姚長。

translations.literal: When Sun Quan was general, Huan served in the headquarters staff and was appointed magistrate of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: While Sun Quan still held the rank of general, Zhu Huan served on his staff and became magistrate of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 往遇疫癘，谷食荒貴，桓分部良吏，隱親醫藥，餐粥相繼，士民感戴之。

translations.literal: When he went there he encountered pestilence; grain food was scarce and dear; Huan divided his duties among good clerks, personally tended the sick with medicine, and gruel followed one bowl after another, so officers and commoners were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: A plague struck the county and grain soared in price; Zhu Huan split the work among able officers, fed the sick gruel and physic himself, and won the people's devotion.

sentences.zh: 遷蕩寇校尉，授兵二千人，使部伍吳、會二郡，鳩合遺散，期年之間，得萬餘人。

translations.literal: He was promoted to colonel who smashes bandits, was given two thousand soldiers, and ordered to organize Wu and Kuaiji commanderies, gathering scattered refugees, and within the space of a year obtained more than ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to colonel who smashes bandits, took two thousand men, and recruited stragglers across Wu and Kuaiji until he had over ten thousand within a year.

sentences.zh: 後丹楊、鄱陽山賊蜂起，攻沒城郭，殺略長吏，處處屯聚。

translations.literal: Later mountain bandits of Danyang and Poyang sprang up like bees, attacked and overthrew walled towns, killed and plundered chief officials, and encamped everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Then Danyang and Poyang bandits swarmed, stormed cities, slew magistrates, and camped in every valley.

sentences.zh: 桓督領諸將，周旋赴討，應皆平定。

translations.literal: Huan directed the generals, wheeling about to attack and punish, and in each case they were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Huan led the generals in swift strikes and stamped them out.

sentences.zh: 稍遷裨將軍，封新城亭候。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to lieutenant general and enfeoffed as village marquis of Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: He stepped up to lieutenant general and village marquis of Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 後代周泰為濡須督。

translations.literal: Later he replaced Zhou Tai as commander at Ruxu.
translations.idiomatic: He later succeeded Zhou Tai as Ruxu commander.

sentences.zh: 黃武元年，魏使大司馬曹仁步騎數萬向濡須，仁欲以兵襲取州上，偽先揚聲欲東攻羨溪；

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangwei Wei sent the grand marshal Cao Ren with several tens of thousands of foot and horse toward Ruxu; Ren wished to use troops to seize the islet in the river and falsely first spread word that he intended to attack east toward Xianxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangwu 1 Wei sent Grand Marshal Cao Ren with tens of thousands toward Ruxu; Cao Ren meant to snatch the midriver islet while crying aloud that he would strike Xianxi to the east.

sentences.zh: 桓分兵將赴羨溪，既發，卒得仁進軍拒濡須七十里問。

translations.literal: Huan divided troops intending to hurry to Xianxi; they had already set out when suddenly word came that Ren was advancing to oppose Ruxu at a distance of seventy li.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Huan split his force for Xianxi, but scouts soon reported Cao Ren already seventy li from Ruxu on the embankment.

sentences.zh: 桓遣使追還羨溪兵，兵未到而仁奄至。

translations.literal: Huan sent messengers to recall the Xianxi troops; the troops had not arrived when Ren suddenly came up.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled the Xianxi column, yet Cao Ren arrived before it returned.

sentences.zh: 時桓手下及所部兵，在者五千人，諸將業業，各有懼心，桓喻之曰："凡兩軍交對，勝負在將，不在眾寡。

translations.literal: At that time the men under Huan's hand and the troops of his command who were present numbered five thousand; the generals were uneasy and each harbored fear, but Huan instructed them, saying, "Whenever two hosts face each other, victory and defeat lie in the commander, not in whether the numbers are many or few.
translations.idiomatic: Only five thousand of Zhu Huan's men stood ready; every general quaked, yet Zhu Huan told them, "When two armies meet, the general decides the day, not the head count.

sentences.zh: 諸君聞曹仁用兵行師，孰與桓邪?兵法所以稱客倍而主人半者，謂俱在平原。

translations.literal: You gentlemen have heard of Cao Ren's use of troops and marching of armies—how does he compare with Huan? What the art of war calls the guest needing double while the host needs only half refers to both sides being on the plain.
translations.idiomatic: You know Cao Ren's reputation in the field—how does it stack against mine? The classic rule that the invader needs twice the strength applies on open ground.

sentences.zh: 無城池之守，又謂士眾勇怯齊等故耳。

translations.literal: Without the defense of walls and moats, and it also means that the courage and cowardice of the soldiers are evenly matched.
translations.idiomatic: It assumes no walled camps and evenly matched nerve.

sentences.zh: 今人既非智勇，加其士卒甚怯，又千里步涉，人馬罷困，桓與諸軍。

translations.literal: Now the enemy commander is neither wise nor brave, his soldiers are deeply timid, and after a thousand-li foot march both men and horses are spent; Zhu Huan and our armies stand ready to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Their general has no genius or nerve, his men are frightened, and a thousand-li slog has broken horse and rider; Zhu Huan and your comrades are ready to meet him.

sentences.zh: 共據高城，南臨大江，北背山陵，以逸待勞，為主制客，此百戰百勝之勢也。

translations.literal: together hold the high city, south overlooking the great river, north backed by hills and tombs, awaiting the weary with the rested, as host controlling guest—this is the posture of a hundred fights and a hundred victories.
translations.idiomatic: We hold this high town with the river at our front and hills at our back, fresh against weary, defender against intruder—that is the posture that wins every fight.

sentences.zh: 雖曹丕自來，尚不足憂，況仁等邪!"桓因偃旗鼓，外示虛弱，以誘致仁。

translations.literal: Even if Cao Pi came in person he would still not be worth worrying about, how much the less Ren and the others!" Huan therefore lowered drums and banners and outwardly displayed weakness to lure Ren.
translations.idiomatic: Were Cao Pi himself to come I would not fret, let alone Cao Ren!" He furled drums and colors and feigned weakness to bait the enemy.

sentences.zh: 仁果遣其子泰攻濡須城，分遣將軍常雕督諸葛虔、王雙等，乘油船別襲中洲。

translations.literal: Ren indeed sent his son Tai to attack the city of Ruxu, separately sending the general Chang Diao to supervise Zhuge Qian, Wang Shuang, and others to ride oil boats in a separate raid on the mid-islet.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ren sent Cao Tai against Ruxu town while Chang Diao, Zhuge Qian, and Wang Shuang skimmed in oiled boats toward the central islet.

sentences.zh: 中洲者，部曲妻子所在也。

translations.literal: The mid-islet was where dependents and families of the host were located.
translations.idiomatic: That islet held the soldiers' wives and children.

sentences.zh: 仁自將萬人留橐皋，復為泰等後拒。

translations.literal: Ren himself led ten thousand men and stayed at Tuogao, again acting as rear guard for Tai and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ren camped ten thousand at Tuogao to backstop Cao Tai.

sentences.zh: 桓部兵將攻取油船，或別擊雕等，桓等身自拒泰，燒營而退，遂梟雕，生虜雙，送武昌，臨陳斬溺死者千餘。

translations.literal: Huan's division of troops attacked and seized the oil boats, or separately struck Diao and the others; Huan and the rest personally resisted Tai, burned the camp and withdrew, then beheaded Diao, captured Shuang alive, sent them to Wuchang, and in the battle line beheaded or drowned more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Huan's men took the oil boats, others fell on Chang Diao, and Zhu Huan himself drove Cao Tai off in flames, took Chang Diao's head, dragged Wang Shuang in bonds to Wuchang, and left a thousand Wei dead in the water and dust.

sentences.zh: 權嘉桓功，封嘉興侯，遷奮武將軍，領彭城相。

translations.literal: Quan praised Huan's achievement, enfeoffed him as marquis of Jiaxing, promoted him to general who rouses martial prowess, and gave him the chancellorship of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan rewarded him with the Jiaxing marquisate, the rank of general who rouses martial prowess, and the titular chancellorship of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 黃武七年，鄱陽太守周魴譎誘魏大司馬曹休，休將步騎十萬至皖城以迎魴。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Huangwu the grand administrator of Poyang, Zhou Fang, deceived and lured Wei's grand marshal Cao Xiu; Xiu led a hundred thousand foot and horse to Wancheng to welcome Fang.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangwu 7 Zhou Fang of Poyang baited Wei's Grand Marshal Cao Xiu, who marched a hundred thousand men to Wancheng to receive him.

sentences.zh: 時陸遜為元帥，全琮與桓為左右督，各督三萬人擊休。

translations.literal: At that time Lu Xun was supreme commander, Quan Zong and Huan were left and right directors, each commanding thirty thousand men to strike Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun held supreme command while Quan Zong and Zhu Huan led thirty thousand each against Cao Xiu.

sentences.zh: 休知見欺，當引軍還，自負眾盛，邀於一戰。

translations.literal: Xiu knew he had been deceived and ought to lead the army back, but trusting in the abundance of his host he challenged them to a single battle.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiu saw the trap and should have withdrawn, yet trusted his numbers and demanded one decisive clash.

sentences.zh: 桓進計曰："休本以親戚見任，非智勇名將也。

translations.literal: Huan advanced a plan, saying, "Xiu was originally appointed through kinship; he is not a commander famed for wisdom and courage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Huan urged, "Cao Xiu owes his post to connections, not to genius in arms.

sentences.zh: 今戰必敗，敗必定。

translations.literal: Now if we fight he is sure to be defeated, and if defeated he is sure to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Fight him and he will break; break and he will run.

sentences.zh: 走當由夾石、掛車，此兩道皆險阨，若以萬兵柴路，則彼眾可盡。

translations.literal: When he flees he must take the roads of Jiashi and Guache; both these roads are perilously narrow, and if with ten thousand men we block the road with felled timber, then that host can be wholly taken.
translations.idiomatic: His retreat must thread Jiashi and Guache—both defiles where ten thousand men felling trees could swallow his whole army.

sentences.zh: 而休可生虜，臣請將所部以斷之。

translations.literal: And Xiu can be captured alive; your subject asks to lead the troops under his command to cut them off.
translations.idiomatic: Give me my command to cut those passes and we may take Cao Xiu alive.

sentences.zh: 若蒙天威，得以休自效，便可乘勝長驅，近取壽春，割有淮面，以規許、洛，此萬世一時，不可失也。

translations.literal: If favored by Heaven's majesty and able to deliver Xiu to Your Majesty's service, then we can exploit victory in a long drive, draw near and take Shouchun, carve out the south bank of the Huai, and aim at Xu and Luo—this is a chance that comes once in ten thousand ages and must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven favors us and Cao Xiu falls into your hands, we can roll forward, seize Shouchun, clip the Huai's south bank, and eye Xuchang and Luoyang—a once-in-ages opening we dare not waste.

sentences.zh: "權先與陸遜議，遜以為不可，故計不施行。

translations.literal: "Quan had first discussed with Lu Xun, and Xun thought it could not be done, and therefore the plan was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan first asked Lu Xun, who vetoed the scheme, so it died in council.

sentences.zh: 黃龍元年，拜桓前將軍，領青州牧，假節。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huanglong he appointed Huan forward general, concurrent shepherd of Qing Province, and lent him the baton of office.
translations.idiomatic: In Huanglong 1 Zhu Huan became forward general, nominal shepherd of Qing Province, and took the baton.

sentences.zh: 嘉禾六年，魏廬江主簿呂習請大兵自迎，欲開門為應。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiahe Wei's chief clerk of Lujiang, Lü Xi, requested a great army to come welcome him and wished to open the gates as inside response.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiahe 6 Lü Xi, chief clerk of Wei's Lujiang, begged Wu to send a relief host and promised to open the gates.

sentences.zh: 桓與衛將軍全琮俱以師迎。

translations.literal: Huan together with the guards general Quan Zong both led the army to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Huan and the guards general Quan Zong marched to meet him.

sentences.zh: 既至，事露，軍當引還。

translations.literal: After they arrived the affair was exposed, and the army ought to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The plot leaked; the expedition had to pull out.

sentences.zh: 城外有溪水，去城一里所，廣三十餘丈，深者八九尺，淺者半之，諸軍勒兵渡去，桓自斷後。

translations.literal: Outside the city was a stream, about one li from the city, more than thirty zhang wide; where deep it was eight or nine chi, where shallow half of that; the various armies drew up troops to cross and leave, while Huan himself covered the rear.
translations.idiomatic: A stream lay a li outside the walls, thirty-odd zhang across, knee-deep in the shallows and deeper in the channel; the columns filed across while Zhu Huan alone covered the rear.

sentences.zh: 時廬江太守李膺整嚴兵騎，欲須諸軍半渡，因迫擊之。

translations.literal: At that time the grand administrator of Lujiang, Li Ying, drew up strict horse and foot, intending to wait until the various armies were half across and then press the attack.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei governor Li Ying massed horse and foot, meaning to strike when half the Wu host was midstream.

sentences.zh: 及見桓節蓋在後，卒不敢出，其見憚如此。

translations.literal: But when he saw Huan's baton and canopy in the rear, in the end he did not dare come out—such was the fear in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw Zhu Huan's banner and credentials still on the far bank he dared not move—that was the dread Zhu Huan inspired.

sentences.zh: 是時全琮為督，權又令偏將軍胡綜宣傳詔命，參與軍事。

translations.literal: At that time Quan Zong was commander, and Quan again ordered the lieutenant general Hu Zong to proclaim the edict's commands and participate in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Zong held overall command while Sun Quan also sent Hu Zong to read edicts and sit on the council of war.

sentences.zh: 琮以軍出無獲，議欲部分諸將，有所掩襲。

translations.literal: Zong, because the army had gone out without gain, deliberated wishing to divide the generals' forces and make a sudden raid somewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Because the campaign won nothing, Quan Zong proposed splitting the generals for a surprise stroke.

sentences.zh: 桓素氣高，恥見部伍，乃往見琮，問行意，感激發怒，與琮校計。

translations.literal: Huan by nature was lofty in spirit and ashamed to be placed under command, and therefore went to see Zong, asked his intentions, was moved to anger, and disputed plans with Zong.
translations.idiomatic: Proud Zhu Huan hated taking orders; he confronted Quan Zong, grew heated, and argued the dispositions.

sentences.zh: 琮欲自解，因曰："上自令胡綜為督，綜意以為宜爾。

translations.literal: Zong wished to excuse himself and therefore said, "His Majesty himself ordered Hu Zong to be commander; Zong thought that was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Zong deflected blame: "The throne named Hu Zong commander; I merely agreed.

sentences.zh: "桓愈恚恨，還乃使人呼綜。

translations.literal: "Huan grew only more resentful, and on returning then sent men to summon Zong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Huan's fury deepened; back in camp he sent for Hu Zong.

sentences.zh: 綜至軍門，桓出迎之，顧謂左右曰："我縱手，汝等各自去。

translations.literal: When Zong reached the army gate, Huan came out to meet him, looked back and said to those at his side, "If I let my hand go, you gentlemen each go your own way.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zong reached the gate; Zhu Huan stepped out, glanced at his attendants, and said, "If I loose my grip, you may scatter.

sentences.zh: "有一人旁出，語綜使還。

translations.literal: "One man stepped aside and told Zong to return.
translations.idiomatic: One man slipped aside and whispered that Hu Zong should leave.

sentences.zh: 桓出，不見綜，知左右所為，因斫殺之。

translations.literal: Huan came out, did not see Zong, knew it was the doing of those at his side, and therefore hacked them to death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Huan emerged, missed Hu Zong, realized his own men had turned the envoy back, and cut them down.

sentences.zh: 桓佐軍進諫，刺殺佐軍，遂托狂發，詣建業治病。

translations.literal: Huan's army adviser remonstrated; he stabbed the army adviser to death, then pretended a fit of madness and went to Jianye to treat his illness.
translations.idiomatic: When his army adviser protested, Zhu Huan killed him too, feigned madness, and rode to Jianye for a cure.

sentences.zh: 權惜其功能，故不罪。

translations.literal: Quan pitied his merit and ability, and therefore did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan valued his service too much to punish him.

sentences.zh: 〈孙盛曰：书云臣无作威作福，作威作福，则凶于而家，害于而国。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng states: The document says a minister must not make awe or make blessing; to make awe and blessing is ill for your house and harmful to your state.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng cites the classic: ministers must not play tyrant or patron; doing so ruins house and state.

sentences.zh: 桓之贼忍，殆虎狼也，人君且犹不可，况将相乎？

translations.literal: Huan's cruelty and ruthlessness were almost those of a tiger or wolf; even for a lord it is still not permissible, how much the less for ministers and generals?
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Huan's savagery was tiger-wolf stuff—intolerable even in a prince, let alone a general?

sentences.zh: 语曰，得一夫而失一国，纵罪亏刑，失孰大焉！〉

translations.literal: As the saying goes, to gain one man and lose a state—though you pardon him and bend the punishment, what loss could be greater!
translations.idiomatic: The proverb says: win one bravo and lose a kingdom—no graver fault than sparing such a crime.

sentences.zh: 使子異攝領部曲，令醫視護，數月復遣還中洲。

translations.literal: He had his son Yi take acting command of the host, ordered physicians to attend and nurse him, and after several months again sent him back to the mid-islet.
translations.idiomatic: He put his son Zhu Yi in charge of his troops, set physicians to watch him, and after a few months sent him back to the islet garrison.

sentences.zh: 權自出祖送，謂曰："今寇虜尚存，王塗未一，孤當與君共定天下，欲令督五萬人專當一面，以圖進取，想君疾未復發也。

translations.literal: Quan personally came out to perform the road sacrifice for him and said, "Now the bandits and enemies still survive and the kingly way is not yet one; I ought with you, sir, to settle the realm under Heaven; I wish to have you command fifty thousand men and hold a single front so as to plan advance; I suppose your illness has not yet recurred.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan walked him to the parting rite and said, "Rebels still live and the realm is not yet one; I had meant to give you fifty thousand men and a whole front of your own—if only your illness does not return.

sentences.zh: "桓曰："天授陛下聖姿，當君臨四海，猥重任臣，以除奸逆，臣疾當自愈。"

translations.literal: Huan said, "Heaven has given Your Majesty a sacred mien; you are meant to rule the four seas. To lay so heavy a burden on your servant to purge traitors and rebels—your servant's illness will surely heal of its own."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Huan answered, "Heaven gave Your Majesty a sovereign's bearing to rule the four seas; loading your servant with the work of scourging traitors will cure whatever ails him."

sentences.zh: 〈吴录曰：桓奉觞曰：“臣当远去，原一捋陛下须，无所复恨。

translations.literal: The Wu lu states: Huan raised a cup and said, "Your subject is about to go far; I beg to stroke once Your Majesty's beard, and then I will have no further regret.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu lu adds: Zhu Huan raised his cup: "I march far; let me tug your beard once and I die content.

sentences.zh: ”权冯几前席，桓进前捋须曰：“臣今日真可谓捋虎须也。

translations.literal: "Quan leaned forward on the armrest toward the mat, and Huan advanced and stroked the beard, saying, "Your subject today may truly be called one who has tugged a tiger's whiskers.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan leaned on the rail; Zhu Huan stepped up, tugged his whiskers, and said, "Today I have truly tweaked the tiger.

sentences.zh: ”权大笑。〉

translations.literal: "Quan laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 桓性護前，恥為人下，每臨敵交戰，節度不得自由，輒嗔恚憤激。

translations.literal: Huan's nature was jealous of precedence and ashamed to be beneath others; whenever he faced the enemy in battle and command and control were not free for him, he would rage and grow fierce with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He could not bear subordination: if orders cramped him in battle he boiled with rage.

sentences.zh: 然輕財貴義，兼以強識。

translations.literal: Yet he held wealth lightly and prized righteousness, and moreover had a powerful memory.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he despised riches, honored duty, and never forgot a face.

sentences.zh: 與人一面，數十年不忘，部曲萬口，妻子盡識之。

translations.literal: With a man one meeting, several decades he did not forget; with a host of ten thousand mouths, wives and children he all recognized them.
translations.idiomatic: One glance decades ago stayed with him; he knew every face among ten thousand dependents.

sentences.zh: 愛養吏士，贍護六親，俸祿產業，皆與共分。

translations.literal: He loved and nurtured clerks and soldiers, supported and protected the six kinds of kin, and salaries and estates he all shared with them.
translations.idiomatic: He fed his soldiers, carried his whole kinship on his pay, and split every stipend.

sentences.zh: 及桓疾困，舉營憂戚。

translations.literal: When Huan's illness grew desperate, the whole camp grieved.
translations.idiomatic: When his last illness came, every tent mourned.

sentences.zh: 年六十二，赤烏元年卒。

translations.literal: In his sixty-second year he died in the first year of Chiwu.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-two in Chiwu 1.

sentences.zh: 吏士男女，無不號慕。

translations.literal: Clerks, soldiers, men and women—none failed to wail and long for him.
translations.idiomatic: Officers, men, women—everyone wept for him.

sentences.zh: 又家無餘財，權賜鹽五千斛以周喪事。

translations.literal: Moreover his household had no surplus wealth, and Quan granted five thousand hu of salt to supply the funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His house was bare; Sun Quan gave five thousand hu of salt to bury him decently.

sentences.zh: 子異嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu Yi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 子 異

translations.literal: Son: Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The heir: Zhu Yi.

sentences.zh: 異字季文，以父任除郎，

translations.literal: Yi, courtesy name Jiwen, by his father's position was appointed gentleman,
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi, styled Jiwen, entered the court as a gentleman through his father's rank,

sentences.zh: 〈文士传曰：张惇子纯与张俨及异俱童少，往见骠骑将军硃据。

translations.literal: The Wen shi zhuan states: Zhang Dun's son Chun, together with Zhang Yan and Yi, were all still boys when they went to see the chief of cavalry Zhu Ju.
translations.idiomatic: The Wen shi zhuan tells how Zhang Chun, Zhang Yan, and Zhu Yi, still boys, once called on Chief of Cavalry Zhu Ju.

sentences.zh: 据闻三人才名，欲试之，告曰：“老鄙相闻，饥渴甚矣。

translations.literal: Ju heard of the three lads' literary reputations and wished to test them, saying to them, "I am old and rustic, but I have heard of you and am parched with thirst for your talent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ju had heard of their budding fame and proposed a trial: "I am a dull old man who has long thirsted for word of you.

sentences.zh: 夫騕褭以迅骤为功，鹰隼以轻疾为妙，其为吾各赋一物，然后乃坐。

translations.literal: The fine steed is prized for swift gallop, the hawk for light speed; each of you compose a rhapsody on one thing for me, and only then may you take your seats.
translations.idiomatic: The swift courser wins praise for its dash, the hawk for its strike—each of you versify whatever your eye falls on, and we dine only after.

sentences.zh: ”俨乃赋犬曰：“守则有威，出则有获，韩卢、宋鹊，书名竹帛。

translations.literal: "Yan then rhapsodized on the dog, saying, "In the kennel it shows awe, abroad it brings game—Han Lu and Song Que, their names are written on bamboo and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan sang the dog: fierce at the door, deadly in the field—like Han Lu and Song Que, names inked on the histories.

sentences.zh: ”纯赋席曰：“席以冬设，簟为夏施，揖让而坐，君子攸宜。

translations.literal: "Chun rhapsodized on the mat, saying, "The mat is spread in winter, the fine bamboo mat in summer; bowing and yielding the seat, this is what suits the gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun took the rush mat: laid in winter, bamboo in summer, yielding the seat—fit for a gentleman.

sentences.zh: ”异赋弩曰：“南岳之幹，锺山之铜，应机命中，获隼高墉。

translations.literal: "Yi rhapsodized on the crossbow, saying, "Timber from the Southern March, bronze from Mount Zhong—release the catch and strike the mark, bring down the hawk on the high wall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi chose the crossbow: wood from the southern ranges, bronze from Bell Mountain—draw, loose, and drop the falcon on the parapet.

sentences.zh: ”三人各随其目所见而赋之，皆成而后坐，据大欢悦。〉

translations.literal: "Each of the three followed what his eyes saw and rhapsodized on it; when all were finished they then sat down, and Ju was greatly delighted.
translations.idiomatic: The three each versified the first object they saw, finished, then took their seats, and Zhu Ju was delighted.

sentences.zh: 後拜騎都尉，代桓領兵，赤烏四年，隨朱然攻魏樊城，建計破其外圍，還拜偏將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed colonel of cavalry, replaced Huan in leading troops, and in the fourth year of Chiwu followed Zhu Ran in attacking Wei's Fancheng of Wei, devised a plan that broke the outer ring of fortifications, and on return was appointed lieutenant general.
translations.idiomatic: He later became colonel of cavalry, inherited Zhu Huan's command, joined Zhu Ran's Chiwu 4 strike on Wei's Fancheng, planned the breach of the outer stockade, and returned a lieutenant general.

sentences.zh: 魏廬江太守文欽營住六安，多設屯寨，置諸道要，以招誘亡叛，為邊寇害。

translations.literal: Wei's grand administrator of Lujiang, Wen Qin, camped at Lu'an, set up many stockades and posts at critical roads, and used them to entice fugitives and rebels, doing harm as a border scourge.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin of Wei stacked camps at Lu'an along every choke point to lure deserters and raid the frontier.

sentences.zh: 異乃身率其手下二千人，掩破欽七屯，斬首數百，遷揚武將軍。

translations.literal: Yi then personally led the two thousand men under his hand, made a surprise attack that broke seven of Qin's camps, beheaded several hundred, and was promoted to general who displays martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi led his two thousand in a night rush, shattered seven of Wen Qin's camps, took several hundred heads, and won promotion as general who displays martial prowess.

sentences.zh: 權與論攻戰，辭對稱意。

translations.literal: Quan discussed attack and defense with him, and his replies matched Quan's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan debated tactics with him and liked every answer.

sentences.zh: 權謂異從父驃騎將軍據曰："本知季文定，見之復過所聞。

translations.literal: Quan said to Yi's uncle by marriage, the chief of cavalry Ju, "Originally I knew Jiwen was steady; seeing him now he surpasses what I heard.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan told Zhu Ju, his kinsman and chief of cavalry, "I always knew Zhu Yi was solid; meeting him he outshines even the reports.

sentences.zh: 十三年，文欽詐降，密書與異，欲令自迎。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Wen Qin feigned surrender and secretly wrote to Yi, wishing to have him come welcome him in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Wen Qin pretended to defect, writing secretly to Zhu Yi to ask him to ride out in person.

sentences.zh: 異表呈欽書，因陳其偽，不可便迎。

translations.literal: Yi memorialized and presented Qin's letter, then set forth that it was false and that he could not lightly go to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi laid the letter before the throne, argued it was a snare, and warned against a hasty welcome.

sentences.zh: 權詔曰："方今北土未一，欽雲欲歸命，宜且迎之。

translations.literal: Quan's edict said, "At present the northern soil is not yet one; Qin says he wishes to submit his allegiance—you should for the time being go welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The edict answered, "The north is still divided; if Wen Qin means to submit, you should meet him for now.

sentences.zh: 若嫌其有譎者，但當設計網以羅之，盛重兵以防之耳。

translations.literal: If you suspect he has deceit, you need only spread nets to catch him in them and mass heavy troops to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: If you fear treachery, set traps and stack the border with heavy arms.

sentences.zh: "乃遣呂據督二萬人，與異並力，至北界，欽果不降。

translations.literal: "Thereupon he sent Lü Ju to direct twenty thousand men to join forces with Yi; they reached the northern border, and Qin indeed did not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Lü Ju with twenty thousand to back Zhu Yi; they reached the frontier and Wen Qin never came over.

sentences.zh: 建興元年，遷鎮南將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianxing he was promoted to general who guards the south.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 1 he became general who guards the south.

sentences.zh: 是歲魏遣胡遵、譜葛誕等出東興，異督水軍攻浮梁，壞之，魏軍大破。

translations.literal: That year Wei sent Hu Zun, Zhuge Dan, and others out against Dongxing; Yi directed the water army to attack the floating bridge, destroyed it, and the Wei army was greatly shattered.
translations.idiomatic: The same year Hu Zun and Zhuge Dan struck Dongxing; Zhu Yi led the river wing, smashed the pontoon, and broke the Wei host.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：异又随诸葛恪围新城，城既不拔，异等皆言宜速还豫章，袭石头城，不过数日可拔。

translations.literal: The Wu shu states: Yi again followed Zhuge Ke in besieging Xincheng; when the city could not be taken, Yi and the others all said they ought quickly to return to Yuzhang and raid Stone City, which could be taken within a few days.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu shu adds: Zhu Yi followed Zhuge Ke at Xincheng; when the siege stalled, he urged a fast return to raid Stone City, which would fall in days.

sentences.zh: 恪以书晓异，异投书於地曰：“不用我计，而用傒子言！

translations.literal: Ke used a letter to instruct Yi; Yi threw the letter on the ground and said, "They do not use my plan but listen to that boy's words!
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke wrote him down; Zhu Yi flung the letter down: "You ignore my counsel for some stripling's whim!

sentences.zh: ”恪大怒，立夺其兵，遂废还建业。〉

translations.literal: "Ke was greatly angry, immediately stripped him of his troops, and then dismissed him to return to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke raged, stripped him of command on the spot, and packed him off to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 太平二年，假節，為大都督，救壽春圍，不解。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping he was lent the baton of office, became grand commander-in-chief, and went to rescue the siege of Shouchun, but the siege was not lifted.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping 2 he took the baton as grand commander and marched to relieve Shouchun without breaking the ring.

sentences.zh: 還軍，為孫綝所枉害。

translations.literal: Returning the army, he was wrongfully harmed by Sun Lin.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home Sun Lin murdered him on a false charge.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：綝要异相见，将往，恐陆抗止之，异曰：“子通，家人耳，当何所疑乎！

translations.literal: The Wu shu states: Lin invited Yi to meet him; as he was about to go, fearing that Lu Kang would stop him, Yi said, "Zitong is family—what is there to doubt!"
translations.idiomatic: The Wu shu says Sun Lin summoned him; Lu Kang would have held him back, but Zhu Yi said, "Zitong is kin—why doubt!"

sentences.zh: ”遂往。

translations.literal: "Thereupon he went.
translations.idiomatic: He went.

sentences.zh: 綝使力人於坐上取之。

translations.literal: Lin had strong men seize him at his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin had brutes drag him from his cushion.

sentences.zh: 异曰：“我吴国忠臣，有何罪乎？

translations.literal: Yi said, "I am a loyal minister of the state of Wu—what crime have I?
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi cried, "I am Wu's loyal servant—what is my crime?

sentences.zh: ”乃拉杀之。〉

translations.literal: "Thereupon they dragged him off and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They hauled him out and killed him.

translations.literal: 【Appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 評曰：朱治、呂范以舊臣任用，朱然、朱桓以勇烈著聞，呂據、朱異、施績鹹有將領之才，克紹堂構。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Zhu Zhi and Lü Fan were employed as old ministers; Zhu Ran and Zhu Huan became famous for fierce courage; Lü Ju, Zhu Yi, and Shi Ji all had the talent of generals and were able to carry on the hall and roof beams their fathers raised.
translations.idiomatic: The historian concludes: Zhu Zhi and Lü Fan rose as old retainers; Zhu Ran and Zhu Huan won fame in battle; Lü Ju, Zhu Yi, and Shi Ji each had a general's gift and could uphold their fathers' houses.

sentences.zh: 若范、桓之越隘，得以吉終，至於據、異無此之尤而反罹殃者，所遇之時殊也。

translations.literal: As for Fan and Huan, who crossed perilous defiles and were able to meet a fortunate end, whereas Ju and Yi had no such excess yet instead suffered disaster—the times they encountered were different.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Fan and Zhu Huan braved deadly ground yet died in honor; Lü Ju and Zhu Yi committed no such outrage yet perished—the difference lay in the times they met, not in their merits alone.
